Generated from windword-labs/gyres-spec at Gyres v0.75.0. Source of each part is marked.


<!-- file: README.md -->

# Gyres spec

这是 Gyres Core 对外接口的公开说明：HTTP 接口、事件流和入门指南，供想给自己运行的 Gyres Core 做前端（网页、手机、命令行）的开发者使用，主要写给编码 Agent 读。全部为英文 Markdown，只描述最新版本。用法：把 `llms.txt`（索引）或 `llms-full.txt`（全部内容合成一个文件）交给你的 Agent，或者从下面的 Guides 开始读。

---

This repository is the contract for building your own frontend for **Gyres
Core**: the HTTP endpoints, the Server-Sent Events streams and short guides.
It is written for coding agents first and humans second. It describes the
latest Gyres release only; breaking changes are listed in
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Start here

- Agents: read [llms.txt](llms.txt) (index) or [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt)
  (every file in one).
- Humans: the [guides](#guides), then the endpoint reference.

## Basics

- Core is an HTTP server the owner runs on their own machine (desktop app or
  standalone `gyresd`). Its address is whatever the owner gives you, for
  example `http://127.0.0.1:15100`, a LAN address, or an `https://` domain.
- Every request except a few marked `Auth: none` sends
  `Authorization: Bearer <access key>`. Keys come from the owner or from
  [device pairing](guides/pairing-and-keys.md). One key, the administrator key,
  may also manage Core (`Auth: admin`); every other key is an ordinary key.
  `GET /v1/identity` tells you which kind you hold.
- Requests and responses are JSON unless an endpoint says otherwise. Ignore
  fields you do not know; Core adds fields without notice.
- Live updates come from two SSE streams: the Core-wide `GET /v1/events` and a
  conversation's `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events`. See [events.md](events.md).
- Check compatibility with `GET /v1/version`: it returns
  `{"version": "<Core version>", "api_version": <integer>}`. `api_version` goes
  up by one on every breaking change; compare it with the number your
  frontend was built for and read [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Owners' Cores
  update themselves, your frontend does not.

## Guides

- [Pairing and access keys](guides/pairing-and-keys.md)
- [List conversations](guides/list-conversations.md)
- [Send a message and stream the reply](guides/send-and-stream.md)
- [Stop a run and reattach to it](guides/stop-and-reattach.md)
- [Tool approvals](guides/approvals.md)

## Reference

- [Errors](errors.md): the error body, coded errors, auth failures.
- [Events](events.md): every SSE event and its fields.
- HTTP endpoints, by area:
  - [External agents](http/agents.md)
  - [Tool approvals](http/approvals.md)
  - [Bot and chat channels](http/bot.md)
  - [Plugins, MCP, hooks, computer use and host screen](http/extensions.md)
  - [Files, attachments and search](http/files.md)
  - [Models and model settings](http/models.md)
  - [Device pairing](http/pairing.md)
  - [Projects and skills](http/projects.md)
  - [Runs: sending, streaming, stopping](http/runs.md)
  - [Scheduled tasks](http/schedules.md)
  - [Conversations](http/sessions.md)
  - [Storage, export and import](http/storage.md)
  - [System](http/system.md)

Every endpoint uses the same layout: `### METHOD /path`, then `Auth:`
(`none`, `any key` or `admin`), `Effect:`, `Request`, `Response`, `Errors` and
`Events`.

## What is not covered

Routes only the Core host itself uses (the desktop shell's own credential,
host-only HTTPS settings, update handoff, internal routes), the OAuth redirect
page and a developer test page are deliberately left out. Plugins may add
their own pages and tools; their contents are not part of this spec.



<!-- file: guides/approvals.md -->

# Tool approvals

Some tool calls wait until a person decides. The request shows up on the run stream and on the Core-wide event stream; `GET /v1/approvals` is the list to render, and `POST /v1/approvals/{approval}/decision` records the decision. Closing the page does not approve, reject, or cancel a waiting request. Any client with a key can decide it.

A call that a grant or the policy already allows does not appear here. Read-only calls, the `subagent` tool, and a fixed set of list and read actions never ask.

## 1. Notice a waiting request

On the run stream, a frame with `"type":"approval"` carries the request. `status` `pending` is a card to show. The same shape is sent again when the request is decided. `id` is 32 lowercase hex characters.

```json
{
  "type": "approval",
  "approval": {
    "id": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90",
    "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
    "run_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
    "tool_call_id": "call_01",
    "tool": "exec_command",
    "resource": "{\"command\":\"printf hello\"}",
    "input": { "command": "printf hello" },
    "cwd": "/work/demo",
    "unattended": false,
    "status": "pending",
    "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

Show `tool_label` when it is present, otherwise `tool`. `resource` is the target text (for `write` and `edit`, the absolute file path). `input` is the tool arguments. `once_only: true` means this card cannot be covered by a grant: offer only allow-once and reject.

The Core-wide stream does not include the request. It sends `approvals.changed` with no `session_id`, including more than once for one request. Refetch the list. The stored request can still change after the last `approval` frame.

```bash
curl -N -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/events
```

```
data: {"type":"approvals.changed"}
```

## 2. Load the list

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/approvals?session_id=2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789&offset=0"
```

`200` includes:

- `pending` — how many requests are `pending`, across every conversation.
- `pending_requests` — those requests, newest first. Not paged, and not filtered by `session_id`. Filter this array yourself when the card belongs to one conversation. Render these.
- `requests` — one page of history, every status, newest `created_at` first. `session_id` keeps only rows for that conversation. The page holds at most 100. There is no page-size parameter.
- `total` — the filtered history count. `next_offset` is the next `offset`; it equals `total` on the last page. A missing, negative, or non-integer `offset` counts as 0.
- `state.config` — `mode` is `ask`, `edit`, or `allow` (initial `ask`). `unattended` is `deny`, `wait`, or `allow` (initial `deny`).
- `state.session_modes` — conversation id to `ask`, `edit`, or `allow`. A missing entry inherits `config.mode`.
- `state.grants` — remembered allows. `scope` `global` omits `session_id`. `scope` `session` includes it.

`status` on a request is `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `denied`, `expired`, or `cancelled`. `scope` on an approved request is `once`, `session`, or `global`. `finished_at` is set once it leaves `pending`.

`503` means approvals are not running, or approval storage is unavailable.

## 3. Decide

`scope` is `once`, `session`, `global`, or `reject`. Unknown fields are ignored. The body is at most 4096 bytes.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scope":"once"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/approvals/a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90/decision
```

`200`:

```json
{ "ok": true }
```

- `once` approves that request and stores no grant.
- `reject` records `rejected` with reason `rejected by user`. Other waiting requests stay. The call does not run.
- `session` stores a session grant and approves every other waiting request that grant covers. The grant's conversation is the request's `session_id`.
- `global` stores a grant with no `session_id` and approves every waiting request it covers.
- `once_only: true` ignores `session` and `global`: the request is approved `once`, and no grant is stored.

The response does not include the tool result. An approved call continues inside the run. Refetch `GET /v1/approvals` after `approvals.changed`. `DELETE /v1/approval-grants/{grant}` removes one grant (`200` `{"ok":true}`) and expires every waiting request, not only the ones that grant covered.

## 4. Set the conversation's approval mode

This overrides `config.mode` for one conversation. `mode` is `ask`, `edit`, or `allow`. An empty string, or a JSON object with no `mode`, clears the override so the conversation inherits the global mode.

```bash
curl -sS -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"mode":"allow"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/approval-mode
```

`200` is `{"ok":true}`. When the stored override actually changes, waiting requests for this conversation expire and are not run under the new mode. Reason: `conversation approval mode changed; retry the operation`. Sending the mode already stored changes nothing. A child conversation cannot set its own mode (`409`, message `子任务权限跟随父对话，请在父对话调整`); change the parent. A request with `policy_session` uses that parent's mode.

`ask` asks unless a grant covers the call. `edit` does the same and also allows `write` and `edit` inside the conversation's working directory or a workspace root. `allow` allows the attended call without asking. `once_only` is never covered by a mode or a grant. `PUT /v1/approval-settings` with `{"mode":"ask","unattended":"deny"}` replaces the global policy and expires every waiting request when the stored policy changes.

## 5. User questions

A question is not an approval. The run asks and waits. `GET /v1/events` sends `session.question` with `session_id` and `question_id`. The run stream sends `user_question` with the same batch id. Questions live only in memory.

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/user-questions
```

`200` is `{"questions":[...]}`. Each batch has `id` (a UUID), `tool_call_id`, `questions` (1 to 3), `created`, and `deadline`. Each question has `id`, `header`, `question`, and `options` (2 or 3 of `label` and `description`). Use `deadline`. It is 60 seconds after `created`, unless a longer wait was started. After it, the turn continues with the first option of each question and the batch disappears.

Answer every question in the batch before the deadline. The value does not have to be one of the option labels.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"answers":{"library":"net/http"}}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/user-questions/018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3c/answer
```

`200` is `{"ok":true}`. The run stream then sends `user_question_resolved` with `source` `user` or `timeout`, and `answers` mapping each question id to the chosen label. `source` `cancelled` means the wait was cancelled. `409` `question already resolved` or `question not found` means the batch is gone; refetch the list.

## Edge cases

- `409` `invalid approval scope` — `scope` was missing or not one of the four values.
- `409` `approval is no longer pending` — unknown id, already decided, or already expired. Refetch.
- `409` `context canceled` or `context deadline exceeded` — the run was cancelled. The record is `cancelled`.
- A check can expire the request before your decision (`409`), including `working directory changed while waiting for approval` and `file changed while waiting for approval`. The record is `expired` and `reason` is that message.
- A restart stores a still-waiting request as `expired` with reason `Core restarted; this operation was not replayed`.
- Unattended `deny` stores the request as `denied` and does not ask. Unattended `wait` leaves it `pending`. Unattended `allow` runs it with no request. `unattended: false` is still present on a normal card.
- `400` means the body is not one JSON object of at most 4096 bytes.

## See also

- [Tool approvals](../http/approvals.md) — `GET /v1/approvals`, `POST /v1/approvals/{approval}/decision`, `PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/approval-mode`
- [approvals.changed](../events.md#approvalschanged) and the run-stream [approval](../events.md#approval) frame
- [session.question](../events.md#sessionquestion), [user_question](../events.md#user_question), [GET /v1/sessions/{id}/user-questions](../http/runs.md#get-v1sessionsiduser-questions), [POST …/answer](../http/runs.md#post-v1sessionsiduser-questionsqidanswer)
- [Errors](../errors.md)


<!-- file: guides/list-conversations.md -->

# List conversations

The conversation list is one JSON array from `GET /v1/sessions`. There is no page size, offset, or cursor: replace the list you show with `sessions` on every successful read. Keep it current from the Core-wide event stream, then open one row with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` (or the text transcript) and create a row with `POST /v1/sessions`.

`{id}` is a session id such as `2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789`, or that id, `~`, and a lane name for a side lane. The list contains only main conversations. Bot conversations, and a child whose parent still exists, are omitted. Do not parse ids.

## 1. Load the live list

The only query parameter is `archived`. Omitted, or any value other than the exact string `true`, returns the live list. Rows are newest `modified` first. Pinned rows stay in that order; `pinned_at` is only a marker.

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions
```

`200`:

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "path": "/data/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789.jsonl",
      "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
      "created": "2026-10-14T12:04:05.000Z",
      "modified": "2026-10-14T12:10:00.000Z",
      "message_count": 4,
      "first_message": "Sketch the layout",
      "title": "Layout",
      "pinned_at": "2026-10-14T12:06:00.000Z",
      "running": false,
      "run_state": "idle",
      "unseen": ""
    }
  ]
}
```

Address the row by `session_id`. `title` is omitted when no custom title is stored; show `first_message` then. `pinned_at` is omitted when the row is not pinned. `running` is true while that lane has a live run, including a paused one. `run_state` is `idle`, `running`, `pausing`, `paused`, `waiting_children`, `interrupted`, or `blocked`. A row can have `running: true` and `run_state: "paused"`. `unseen` is `""`, `result`, or `failed`. `workspace`, `scheduled`, and `origin` appear only when set. An empty list is `"sessions": []`.

`archived=true` is the archived list, newest `archived_at` first. Those rows have `archived_at` and `bytes`, and omit `path`, `running`, `run_state`, `unseen`, `pinned_at`, `workspace`, and `origin`.

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions?archived=true"
```

## 2. Keep the list fresh

Open `GET /v1/events` and leave it open. The first frame is `ready`. Each later notification is one `data:` line of JSON and a blank line. There is no `id:` line and no resume cursor. A dropped connection starts again at `ready`. Ignore lines that start with `:` (a `: heartbeat` arrives about every 20 seconds). A `type` you do not know is safe to ignore.

```bash
curl -N -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/events
```

```
data: {"type":"ready","version":"1.4.0","instance_id":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","publishes":["session.task","bot.changed","session.agent_usage","tls.changed"]}

data: {"type":"sessions.changed","session_id":"2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789"}

data: {"type":"session.task","session_id":"2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789"}
```

Refetch the whole list on:

- `sessions.changed` — created, deleted, archived, unarchived, pinned, unpinned, forked, renamed, a lane closed, a generated title, or an unseen run marked seen. `session_id` is the handle. Also refresh the title of that conversation if it is open.
- `session.run_started` and `session.run_finished` — the list's running state. `run_id`, when present, is `task_` plus 32 hex characters. On `session.run_finished`, also reload that conversation if it is open. The run stream closes on its own.
- `session.task` — run state, waiting messages, or child tasks changed. Refetch the list, and if that conversation is open also `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/run-state` and `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/pending-messages`. This event is optional: a Core sends it when `ready.publishes` lists it. Older Cores omit `publishes` and do not send `session.task`. `session.run_started` and `session.run_finished` still refresh running state.

`session.messages` means the transcript grew. It is frequent during a run. Reload `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` only when you are not already following that run's stream.

`resync` means this subscriber's queue overflowed and events were missed. Refetch the list and every open conversation. `503` with `Core is reloading` means connect again.

## 3. Open one conversation

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
```

`200`:

```json
{
  "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
  "records": [],
  "running": false,
  "run_state": "idle",
  "executor": "gyres",
  "history_version": "0-0"
}
```

`records` is the timeline, oldest first, including context records the list skips. Each record has `id`, `ts`, and `message` (`role` `user`, `assistant`, or `tool_result`, and `content`). `turn` is omitted when the record is not part of a turn; `status` is `running` until the turn finishes, then `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or `interrupted`. Compare `history_version`; do not parse it. `history_cursor`, when present, is what a later reattach sends for an external-agent turn. `executor` is `gyres`, or `codex`, `grok`, `pi`, or `claude`. `404` means that id does not exist.

For a text-only view, `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/transcript` returns `records` of `{id, ts, role, text}` plus `transcript_size`, `truncated`, and `omitted`. It has no turns, metadata, or usage. The newest records that fit are kept; `truncated: true` means `omitted` records were left out. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## 4. Create one

The body is ignored. Success is `200` and then `sessions.changed`:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions
```

```json
{ "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789" }
```

Refetch the list, or insert this id and open it. A `500` means the conversation was not left in place.

## Edge cases

- A live row with `running: false` can still have `run_state` `interrupted`, `paused`, or `blocked`. Open it and read run-state before offering a new send.
- `title` missing is normal. `first_message` may be `""`.
- A side lane is not a list row. Open it as `{session_id}~{lane}` on `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`. The lane name is 1 to 48 characters, `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`, and is never `main`.
- `500` on the list means the read failed. Retrying a `GET` is safe.
- While Core is reloading, a new `GET /v1/events` is `503`. An open stream ends; connect again. The same `503` can mean the data directory is unavailable, slow, or moving (`storage_unavailable`, `storage_maintenance`, `storage_slow`).

## See also

- [Conversations](../http/sessions.md) — `GET /v1/sessions`, `POST /v1/sessions`, `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`, `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/transcript`
- [GET /v1/events](../http/runs.md#get-v1events) and [Core-wide events](../events.md#core-wide-events-get-v1events) (`ready`, `resync`, `sessions.changed`, `session.task`, `session.run_started`, `session.run_finished`, `session.messages`)
- [Errors](../errors.md)


<!-- file: guides/pairing-and-keys.md -->

# Pairing and access keys

Almost every Core route needs an access key. The owner can give you one, or an administrator can mint a one-time pairing code that this device redeems for its own ordinary key. Store that secret, send it as `Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY`, then read your role and check `api_version` before you build the rest of the UI.

Set `GYRES_KEY` to the secret you stored. The examples below use `http://127.0.0.1:15100`. A real Core may be a LAN address or an `https://` origin; `GET /v1/identity` lists the origins this Core publishes.

## 1. Use a key the owner gives you

Put the secret in the client's credential store and export it for the examples:

```bash
export GYRES_KEY='the-secret-the-owner-gave-you'
```

An ordinary key and the administrator key use the same header. The administrator key is the only one that can create a pairing code.

## 2. Or pair this device

Pairing only adds a key. It does not list, rename, revoke, or regenerate keys, and the new key is not an administrator key.

An administrator creates one code. The request has no body. The response is `201`:

```bash
curl -sS -D - -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/pairing
```

```json
{
  "code": "K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PAMZXC7HJSBD",
  "core_url": "http://192.0.2.10:15100",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-14T12:02:00Z",
  "id": "K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PA"
}
```

Show `code` to the device. It is 26 characters from the base32 alphabet (`A–Z` and `2–7`), returned only here. `id` (16 characters from that alphabet) is how you poll and cancel; it cannot be redeemed. `expires_at` is two minutes after creation. `core_url` is the address the device should call. At most five codes are active. Each works once. Restarting Core drops every code.

Poll until the device has redeemed it. An unknown id is `expired`, not `404`.

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/pairing/K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PA/status
```

```json
{ "state": "pending" }
```

`state` becomes `redeemed` after a successful redeem, and the body then includes `name`. `expired` means the code lapsed, was cancelled, or is unknown.

The device redeems with no access key. Letter case does not matter; surrounding whitespace is ignored. `device_name` is optional.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/pairing/redeem \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"code":"K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PAMZXC7HJSBD","device_name":"iPhone"}'
```

`201`:

```json
{
  "key_id": "0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "name": "iPhone · 10月4日",
  "secret": "gyres_0123456789abcdef01234567_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

`secret` is shown only in this response. It is `gyres_`, then `key_id` (24 lowercase hex characters), then `_`, then 64 lowercase hex characters. `name` is the cleaned label, then ` · `, then Core's local month and day. If `device_name` is empty, Core derives a label from the `User-Agent` header.

## 3. Store the secret

Replace `GYRES_KEY` with `secret` and keep it in the client's own credential store. Later requests send:

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/identity
```

## 4. Read the role

`GET /v1/identity` (`200`, `Cache-Control: no-store`):

```json
{
  "role": "admin",
  "host": "studio",
  "instance_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "addresses": [
    { "url": "https://core.example.com", "source": "https" },
    { "url": "http://192.0.2.10:15100", "source": "lan" },
    { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:15100", "source": "loopback" }
  ]
}
```

`role` is `admin` or `user`. Hide administrator-only actions when it is `user`. `instance_id` is stable for this Core across restarts (empty when it cannot be stored). `addresses` is never null; `loopback` is always present. Use `instance_id` to tell two addresses of one machine apart.

## 5. Check compatibility

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/version
```

```json
{ "version": "dev", "api_version": 1 }
```

`version` is the Core build (`dev` on a development build, otherwise its version string). `api_version` is an integer and goes up by one on every breaking change. A frontend built for N works with a Core that reports N. When Core reports a higher number, read the entries above N in [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md). A `404` on this route means the Core is older than this spec. Ignore JSON fields you do not know; Core adds fields without notice.

## 6. Handle 401

A missing `Authorization: Bearer` header, an unknown key, or a revoked key is `401` with the plain-text body `unauthorized`. Read the status, not the body: this response is not JSON. Clear the stored secret and ask the owner for a key, or pair again. A key revoked while a request or stream is open ends that request within about a quarter of a second.

## Edge cases

- `POST /v1/pairing` with an ordinary key is `403` and the JSON message `administrator key required`.
- Core that only listens on this computer returns `409` and stores no code. The body is not the usual error envelope:

```json
{
  "code": "loopback_only",
  "error": "Core only listens on this computer; phones cannot connect"
}
```

- `429` on create means five codes are already active. `429` on redeem means ten failed attempts from this client address in ten minutes; the response sets `Retry-After: 600`, and a correct code is refused too while the limit applies.
- `410` on redeem means the code is invalid, expired, or already used. The body is the same for all three, and each counts as a failed attempt.
- `500` `could not create access key` means the code was already consumed. Redeeming again is `410`. Status shows `redeemed` with `name` `""`.
- `400` on redeem means the body is not one JSON object of `code` and `device_name`, or is larger than 4096 bytes.
- `DELETE /v1/pairing/{id}` (administrator) cancels an unused code and returns `204`. A redeemed code stays redeemed.
- While Core is still opening, `GET /v1/identity` and `GET /v1/version` wait up to 10 seconds and may then answer `503` with `code` `core_starting` and `Retry-After: 5`. That starting answer does not require a key. These two routes keep answering while the data directory is unavailable or being moved.
- `403` with the plain-text body `invalid host` means the `Host` header is not an IP address, `localhost`, or Core's configured HTTPS domain.

## Before sending the key to a new address

Once paired, a client usually knows several addresses for its Core (`addresses` from `GET /v1/identity`, local-network discovery). Before it sends the key to an address it did not just use, it can ask that address to prove it holds the key: `POST /v1/identity/challenge` with the key id, a fresh nonce and the origin it is calling, no key attached. Verify the HMAC with your own key and check `instance_id`; send the key only when both match. For a newly discovered address also require `target_ok` true. A Core older than this route answers `401`. Details and test vectors: [POST /v1/identity/challenge](../http/system.md#post-v1identitychallenge).

## See also

- [Device pairing](../http/pairing.md)
- [GET /v1/identity](../http/system.md#get-v1identity) and [GET /v1/version](../http/system.md#get-v1version)
- [Authentication and access errors](../errors.md#authentication-and-access-errors) and [coded errors](../errors.md#coded-errors)
- [Changelog](../CHANGELOG.md)


<!-- file: guides/send-and-stream.md -->

# Send a message and stream the reply

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns` starts one turn and returns its progress as `text/event-stream`. Closing that response does not stop the turn. Render text and tool calls from the frames, and when this conversation is already running, add a follow-up with `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` instead of starting a second turn.

The id below is a session id. A lane is that id, `~`, and a lane name. Codex, Grok, pi, and Claude run only on the main lane.

## 1. Start a turn

The body is JSON. `prompt` is required unless `attachments` is non-empty. Omit `provider_id` and `model` to use the conversation's model, then the settings default, then the first available model.

```bash
curl -N -sS -D - -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Fix the parser and add a test"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/turns
```

Success is `200` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Save the response header `X-Gyres-Run-Stream` (16 lowercase hex characters). Each stored frame is a `data:` line of JSON, an `id:` line (a decimal offset), and a blank line. About every 10 seconds the stream sends `: heartbeat`, which has no `id`. Ignore lines that start with `:`. The stream stays open until the turn finishes. This response always starts at the beginning of the turn.

```
data: {"type":"run_snapshot","session_id":"2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789","records":[]}
id: 128

data: {"type":"text_delta","text":"Looking at the parser."}
id: 196

data: {"type":"tool_start","call":{"id":"call_1","name":"read","input":{"path":"parser.go"}}}
id: 280

data: {"type":"tool_end","call":{"id":"call_1","name":"read","input":{"path":"parser.go"}},"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"ok"}],"is_error":false}}
id: 420

data: {"type":"message_complete","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn","usage":{"input_tokens":12,"output_tokens":4,"cache_read_tokens":0,"cache_write_tokens":0},"error_message":null}}
id: 640

data: {"type":"result","session_id":"2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789","stop_reason":"end_turn"}
id: 780
```

The turn is accepted before the stream is attached. The call is not idempotent: after an ambiguous failure, `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` before you send again. Core also emits `session.run_started`, and when the turn ends `session.run_finished`, on `GET /v1/events`.

## 2. Render the frames

Apply frames in order. Ignore a `type` you do not know.

- `run_snapshot` — replace the transcript on screen with `records`, then apply later frames. `records` match `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`.
- `agent_start` / `turn_start` — a run and a model step are starting. `turn` starts at 1.
- `text_delta` — append `text`. `thinking_delta` — append `thinking`.
- `tool_input_delta` — append `partial_json` to the call `id`. The first fragment includes `name`.
- `tool_start` — show `call` (`id`, `name`, `input`) as running. `input` is `null` when there are no arguments.
- `tool_end` — show `result.content` and `result.is_error` on that call. A call cut off at the output cap can send `tool_end` without `tool_start`.
- `tool_blocked` — the call did not run. Show `reason` when it is present.
- `message_complete` — replace this step's streamed text with `message`. `error_message` is `null` or a string. `stop_reason` is `end_turn`, `tool_use`, `max_tokens`, `error`, or `aborted`.
- `usage` — token counts for the step. Stored totals still come from the usage routes.
- `steering_message` — a user message entered between steps. Show `message`. A `metadata.internalMessage` row is Core's own text.
- `result` — the outcome, and the last stored frame of a normal finish. `stop_reason` is `end_turn`, `error`, or `aborted`. `error` is omitted on `end_turn` and `aborted`. When the stream then closes, reload `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`.
- `approval` and `user_question` — see [Tool approvals](approvals.md). `output_discarded` (`reason` `overflow`) drops the reply streamed since the last stored row; a following `run_snapshot` replaces the view.

`agent_end` finishes the loop. Wait for `result`, then reload the conversation. `stream_error` is not stored, has no `id`, and the response then ends. The turn itself continues; reload the conversation and reattach if it is still running ([Stop a run and reattach](stop-and-reattach.md)).

## 3. When a turn is already running

`409` with the message `turn already running` (for an external agent, `turn already running or awaiting recovery`) means a turn is live. Do not start another. Queue a follow-up. The body has no mode field. Core stores it as `steer` or `queue` from the current running-input setting. A missing setting is `steer`. A Grok turn always stores `queue`. `steer` can enter at the next step. `queue` waits until the current work takes a follow-up.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"queued_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","prompt":"Also check the tests"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/messages
```

`200`:

```json
{
  "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
  "queued": true,
  "id": "queued_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

`id` is optional, at most 128 characters. Send the same id on a retry; the same content is accepted again and does not create a second message. A different body with that id is `409` `message id already used`. `queued` is true both when the message is waiting and when this id was already accepted. Read the mode that was stored:

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/pending-messages
```

`messages[].mode` is `steer` or `queue`. The same route is how you show the waiting list. `GET /v1/running-input-settings` returns the setting (`{"mode":"steer"}` or `{"mode":"queue"}`); `PUT` the same path with that body changes it for later follow-ups.

A different `409` means nothing is live, so `POST …/messages` will also fail (`no active turn ready for input`). The body is not the usual error envelope:

```json
{
  "error": "Gyres is waiting to be continued; continue or stop it first",
  "code": "awaiting_continuation",
  "agent": "Gyres",
  "state": "interrupted"
}
```

`agent` is `Gyres`, `Codex`, `Grok`, `pi`, or `Claude`. `state` is the run state. Continue with `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/resume` or stop with `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel`, then send a new turn.

## 4. Attach an image

Upload the raw image bytes (not multipart) before the turn. `Content-Type` is ignored. At most 20 MiB. PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP only.

```bash
curl -sS -D - -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  --data-binary @photo.png \
  "http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/attachments?name=photo.png"
```

`201` when the bytes are new, `200` when they were already stored:

```json
{
  "id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "name": "photo.png",
  "mime_type": "image/png",
  "size": 12345
}
```

`id` is 64 lowercase hex characters. Pass it as `attachments` on the turn or the follow-up: `{"prompt":"What is in this image?","attachments":["<id>"]}`. A prompt may be `""` when `attachments` is non-empty. At most 20 images and 40 MiB together. A model that does not accept images is rejected. The same limits apply to `POST …/messages`.

## Edge cases

- `400` `missing prompt` when both the prompt and `attachments` are empty. Whitespace-only prompts are rejected for Codex, Grok, pi, and Claude unless there is an image.
- `409` `子会话请通过父任务追加工作` — this conversation is a child; send further work from the parent.
- `409` `任务尚未完成，请先继续或停止` — a task is still open.
- `409` `{"error":"stopped before the turn started","code":"turn_stopped"}` — nothing was recorded.
- `409` while the turn is still preparing: `POST …/messages` returns `no active turn ready for input`. Retry shortly.
- `403` on a Codex, Grok, pi, or Claude conversation asks an administrator to allow non-administrators. An ordinary key still runs a provider-model turn.
- `404` `session not found`. `503` `storage unavailable; reconnect and retry` or Core is moving its data directory.
- Keep `X-Gyres-Run-Stream` and the last `id:` so a dropped connection can resume. That is [Stop a run and reattach](stop-and-reattach.md).

## See also

- [POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns](../http/runs.md#post-v1sessionsidturns) and [POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages](../http/runs.md#post-v1sessionsidmessages)
- [GET /v1/running-input-settings](../http/models.md#get-v1running-input-settings)
- [POST /v1/sessions/{id}/attachments](../http/files.md#post-v1sessionsidattachments)
- [Run events](../events.md#run-events-get-v1sessionsidevents) — `text_delta`, `tool_start`, `tool_end`, `message_complete`, `result`
- [Errors](../errors.md)


<!-- file: guides/stop-and-reattach.md -->

# Stop a run and reattach to it

A turn keeps running after the client that started it disconnects. Stop it only with `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel`. Anyone, including that client after a dropped connection, attaches with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events`. When the stream ends, reload the transcript.

The id in the examples is `2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789`.

## 1. Stop

The request has no body.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/cancel
```

`200`:

```json
{
  "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
  "canceled": true
}
```

`canceled` is always true on success. The HTTP response can arrive before the run stream has closed. Child tasks of this turn are stopped too. When the turn belongs to a scheduled task, that occurrence is cancelled. Core emits `session.task` and `session.run_finished` on `GET /v1/events`.

A second stop, once nothing is left, is `409` `no active turn`. `404` means the conversation does not exist. `500` `task stopped, but cancellation could not be saved: …` means the turn was still stopped.

## 2. Read run-state until it is idle

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/run-state
```

`200`:

```json
{ "state": "running", "reason": "" }
```

`state` is `idle`, `running`, `pausing`, `paused`, `waiting_children`, `interrupted`, or `blocked`. `reason` is always present and may be `""`. After a successful cancel, follow this route or the run stream until the live turn has left. `state` is then `idle`. Also refetch when `session.task` arrives for this conversation.

`interrupted` means the task stopped and can be continued (`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/resume`). `blocked` means it cannot continue until the owner acts. `paused` is waiting for `resume` or `cancel`. A `204` from the event stream (below) does not by itself mean `idle`.

## 3. Reattach with stream and after

Pass the `X-Gyres-Run-Stream` value you saved (16 lowercase hex characters) and the `id:` of the last frame you handled. Both are required together. The server does not read a last-event id header.

```bash
curl -N -sS -D - \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/events?stream=a1b2c3d4e5f60718&after=128"
```

While a turn is running the response is `200` `text/event-stream`, again with `X-Gyres-Run-Stream`. A matching cursor starts with `run_resume` and no `id:`:

```
data: {"type":"run_resume","session_id":"2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789"}

data: {"type":"text_delta","text":"Still working."}
id: 256
```

Keep the transcript you already show, then apply only the frames after `run_resume`. Each later stored frame has an `id:`. Heartbeats (`: heartbeat`, about every 10 seconds) do not. `stream` and `after` are accepted only for this turn's own stream, and only when `after` is the end of a frame.

If the cursor does not match, the stream replays the turn from the beginning. The first stored frame is `run_snapshot`. Replace what you show with its `records` before you apply later frames.

The response stays open until the turn finishes or you disconnect. Close without a `result` frame is a dropped connection: reconnect with the same `stream` and the last `id:` you handled. If the progress log breaks, one frame arrives and the response ends:

```json
{ "type": "stream_error", "error": "progress stream unavailable; reload conversation" }
```

That frame has no `id`. The turn is not cancelled. Reload `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`, and attach again if `running` is still set.

## 4. Or resume an external-agent turn with history_cursor

`history_cursor` is the field on `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`. It resumes a Codex, Grok, pi, or Claude turn after the transcript you loaded. A Gyres turn does not resume this way; use `stream` and `after`.

```bash
curl -N -sS \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/events?history_cursor=CURSOR"
```

Replace `CURSOR` with the `history_cursor` you just received. Do not invent one. Query order: `stream` and `after` are tried first; if they do not match, `history_cursor` is tried; anything else replays from `run_snapshot`. A matching cursor yields `run_resume`, then events after that mark. Keep the history you loaded. Approvals and questions that were not saved in the transcript are not resent; read `GET /v1/approvals` and `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/user-questions`.

## 5. 204 means nothing is live

When nothing is running, including a task that is paused, blocked, or interrupted but not live, the response is `204` with no body. The header `X-Gyres-History-Version` is the same opaque string as `history_version` on `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`. Compare it with the transcript you just loaded. The same value means nothing ran in between.

```bash
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789/events
```

Then read `run-state`. If you still need to continue or stop a waiting task, that route is the one that says `interrupted`, `paused`, or `blocked`.

`409` `turn is preparing; retry observation` means a turn is starting and has no stream yet. Retry the GET.

## 6. Reload the transcript after the end

A normal finish delivers the remaining frames and closes. The last stored frame is `result` when the run published one. The next `GET …/events` is `204`. Reload once:

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GYRES_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:15100/v1/sessions/2026-10-14T12-04-05_3f2a1b0c-4d5e-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
```

That body is the authoritative transcript. `session.run_finished` on `GET /v1/events` is the signal for every other client. Frame fields are in the events reference. Rendering them is covered in [Send a message and stream the reply](send-and-stream.md).

## Edge cases

- `404` `session not found` on cancel, run-state, and the event stream.
- A replay that starts at `run_snapshot` replaces the on-screen transcript. `run_resume` does not.
- `history_cursor` from an earlier turn, a missing cursor, or a Gyres turn falls through to a full replay.
- Pausing is a different route (`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/pause`). Codex, Grok, pi, and Claude have no pause; stop them with cancel.
- Revoking the access key that started a live turn stops it.

## See also

- [POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel](../http/runs.md#post-v1sessionsidcancel), [GET /v1/sessions/{id}/run-state](../http/runs.md#get-v1sessionsidrun-state), [GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events](../http/runs.md#get-v1sessionsidevents)
- [SSE framing](../events.md#sse-framing) and [run events](../events.md#run-events-get-v1sessionsidevents) (`run_resume`, `run_snapshot`, `result`, `stream_error`)
- [GET /v1/sessions/{id}](../http/sessions.md#get-v1sessionsid)
- [session.run_finished](../events.md#sessionrun_finished) and [session.task](../events.md#sessiontask)
- [Errors](../errors.md)


<!-- file: http/agents.md -->

# External agents

External agents are Codex, Grok, pi and Claude Code installed on the computer that runs Core. A conversation can be handed to one of them. These routes save that setup, report whether the program is installed and signed in, report usage for Codex, Grok and Claude, and for Codex, Grok and Claude Code attach a session that was started in a terminal.

The path values are `codex`, `grok`, `pi` and `claude`. Settings and status are Core-wide, one object per agent. Usage splits into the conversation's own totals and the account's quota.

An error from these handlers is `application/json`:

```json
{"error":"invalid Codex settings","failure":{"code":"core_request_failed","message":"invalid Codex settings","http_status":400,"details":"invalid Codex settings"}}
```

`error`, `failure.message` and `failure.details` are the same text. A `500` message can include a path on the Core host.

Settings and status require an administrator key. Their responses, including errors, send `Cache-Control: no-store`. `PUT` replaces the whole settings object: a missing boolean is saved as false, a missing string as empty, and then the rules below run. The body is at most 8192 bytes. A body that is not JSON, has an unknown field, or is larger than that is rejected.

- `enabled`: the agent can run only when true.
- `executable`: empty, or the bare command name (`codex`, `grok`, `pi` or `claude`), means automatic, and is saved as `""`. Core then uses the newest install it finds. Any other value must be an absolute path.
- `approval_scope`: `agent` (one approval covers every operation of that agent) or `operation` (each operation type is remembered separately). Anything else, including empty, is saved as `agent`.
- `allow_members`: when false (the default), an ordinary access key cannot run this agent, and cannot list or attach its terminal sessions.

`allow_unattended`, on Grok and Claude only, defaults to false. While it is false, a scheduled task or a channel message cannot use that agent.

A status response is the last detection, returned immediately, plus:

- `checked_at`: UTC `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`, or `null` until the first detection finishes.
- `checking`: true while a detection is running.
- `step`: `""` when idle. While checking it is `program`, then `account`, then `models`. pi goes from `program` to `models`.
- `executable`: the install the saved settings resolve to right now, or `null` when nothing can run. `auto` is true when the setting is automatic. `version` is omitted when unknown.
- `executables`: every install found right now, or `[]`. `source` is a short label for where it was found. `version` is omitted when unknown.

`path`, `version`, `installed`, `logged_in`, `error` and the model list come from the last finished detection and stay visible while `checking` is true. `error` is omitted when that detection did not fail. `GET` starts a detection only when the agent is enabled and none has finished. `POST` starts one unless one is already running; it does not queue a second. `PUT` starts one, and a detection already running is followed by another so the result matches the settings just saved. Neither request waits for the detection.

`input_tokens` on a usage total includes cached input and cache writes. `cache_write_tokens` is omitted when it is 0. `cost_usd` is the agent's own estimate in USD, not a bill; `cost_source` is `agent_estimate` when `cost_usd` is a number, and both are `null` when the agent gave no estimate. A turn that changes a conversation's usage announces `session.agent_usage` with `session_id`. Reading usage does not.

An account object:

- `kind`: `chatgpt`, `api_key`, `subscription` or `unknown`.
- `plan`: omitted when empty.
- `windows`: rate-limit windows, or `[]`. For Codex, `id` is `5h` for 300 minutes, `weekly` for 10080, otherwise `Nd`, `Nh` or `Nm` from the length, or `primary` / `secondary` when the length is missing. A window with no length and `used_percent` 0 is left out. For Claude, `id` is the limit kind Claude names (`session`, `weekly_all`, `weekly_scoped`, and any later kind as sent), several windows may share an `id`, and there is no `duration_mins`; `label` is the model a scoped limit applies to, `severity` is Claude's level (`normal` or a warning level) and `is_active` is true for the limit Claude marks active. Each of these three is omitted when empty or false, and Codex sends none of them. `resets_at` is UTC, omitted when unknown. `duration_mins` is omitted when unknown.
- `credits`: omitted when the account has none. `balance` is the agent's own credit unit, not a currency, and is omitted when it is not a number. `has_credits` and `unlimited` are booleans.
- `unavailable_reason`: `not_signed_in`, `api_key` or `not_supported`. Omitted when `kind` is `chatgpt` and nothing is wrong. This is why `windows` is empty.
- `updated_at`: UTC time of the last successful read, omitted when there is none.

### GET /v1/codex/settings

Auth: admin
Effect: Returns the Codex settings. When none have been saved, the defaults below.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "executable": "",
  "sandbox": "workspace-write",
  "approval_scope": "agent",
  "approvals_reviewer": "user",
  "allow_members": false
}
```

- `sandbox` is `read-only` or `workspace-write`. The default is `workspace-write`.
- `approvals_reviewer` is `user` (ask the owner) or `auto_review` (Codex's automatic reviewer). The default is `user`. `auto_review` takes effect only when the detected CLI version is at least `0.144.6`; an older or unknown version still asks the owner.

Errors:

- `500` the saved settings cannot be read

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/codex/settings

Auth: admin
Effect: Replaces the Codex settings and starts a detection. The saved object is returned.

Request:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "executable": "",
  "sandbox": "read-only",
  "approval_scope": "operation",
  "approvals_reviewer": "auto_review",
  "allow_members": false
}
```

- `sandbox` is required: `read-only` or `workspace-write`. An empty value is rejected, not replaced with the default.
- `approvals_reviewer` may be omitted or `""`; it is then saved as `user`. Any other value than `user` or `auto_review` is rejected.
- See the shared settings rules for `enabled`, `executable`, `approval_scope` and `allow_members`.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "executable": "",
  "sandbox": "read-only",
  "approval_scope": "operation",
  "approvals_reviewer": "auto_review",
  "allow_members": false
}
```

The body is the saved settings, after automatic executables are stored as `""`, `approval_scope` is normalised, and an empty reviewer is stored as `user`.

Errors:

- `400` invalid Codex settings
- `400` use automatic or an absolute codex executable path
- `400` invalid Codex sandbox
- `400` invalid Codex approval reviewer
- `500` the settings could not be saved

Events: none.

### GET /v1/codex/status

Auth: admin
Effect: Returns the last Codex detection without waiting. Starts one only when Codex is enabled and no detection has finished.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "path": "/usr/local/bin/codex",
  "version": "0.144.6",
  "installed": true,
  "logged_in": true,
  "auth_type": "chatgpt",
  "models": [
    {
      "serviceTiers": [{"id": "standard", "name": "Standard", "description": ""}],
      "defaultServiceTier": "standard",
      "id": "codex-model",
      "model": "codex-model",
      "displayName": "Codex model",
      "isDefault": true,
      "defaultReasoningEffort": "medium",
      "supportedReasoningEfforts": [{"reasoningEffort": "low"}, {"reasoningEffort": "medium"}]
    }
  ],
  "checked_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
  "checking": false,
  "step": "",
  "executable": {"path": "/usr/local/bin/codex", "version": "0.144.6", "auto": true},
  "executables": [{"path": "/usr/local/bin/codex", "version": "0.144.6", "source": "PATH"}]
}
```

- Before the first detection, `installed` and `logged_in` are false, `models` is `[]`, `checked_at` is `null`, and `path`, `version`, `auth_type` and `error` are omitted.
- `logged_in` is true when Codex has an account, or when it does not require a sign-in. `auth_type` is that account's type (`chatgpt` and `apiKey` are the ones Core treats as known) and is omitted when there is no account.
- Model fields keep the names Codex reports. `serviceTiers` and `supportedReasoningEfforts` are `null` when Codex omitted them. `model` is the id a conversation uses; `displayName` is the label.
- A missing program sets `installed` false and `error` to `Codex executable was not found`. A later failure sets `installed` true and `error` to the failure text. Not being signed in leaves `error` omitted.

Errors:

- `500` the saved settings cannot be read
- `500` the status could not be encoded

Events: none.

### POST /v1/codex/status

Auth: admin
Effect: Starts a Codex detection, unless one is already running, and returns the current snapshot immediately. The previous detection stays in the body until the new one finishes; `checking` is then true and `step` starts again at `program`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200` the same object as `GET /v1/codex/status`.

```json
{
  "path": "/usr/local/bin/codex",
  "version": "0.144.6",
  "installed": true,
  "logged_in": true,
  "auth_type": "chatgpt",
  "models": [],
  "checked_at": "2026-10-14T11:00:00Z",
  "checking": true,
  "step": "program",
  "executable": {"path": "/usr/local/bin/codex", "version": "0.144.6", "auto": true},
  "executables": [{"path": "/usr/local/bin/codex", "version": "0.144.6", "source": "PATH"}]
}
```

`models` is the previous list, not cleared at the start of the new detection. With no previous detection, `checked_at` is `null` and the detection fields are the empty ones.

Errors:

- `500` the saved settings cannot be read
- `500` the status could not be encoded

Events: none.

### GET /v1/pi/status

Auth: admin
Effect: Returns the last pi detection without waiting. Starts one only when pi is enabled and no detection has finished. pi has no account: `logged_in` means at least one model can be used.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "path": "/usr/local/bin/pi",
  "version": "0.42.0",
  "installed": true,
  "logged_in": true,
  "providers": ["openai"],
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "openai/pi-model",
      "name": "Pi model",
      "provider": "openai",
      "thinking_levels": ["off", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high"],
      "images": true
    }
  ],
  "checked_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
  "checking": false,
  "step": "",
  "executable": {"path": "/usr/local/bin/pi", "version": "0.42.0", "auto": false},
  "executables": [{"path": "/usr/local/bin/pi", "version": "0.42.0", "source": "PATH"}]
}
```

- `providers` is always an array, `[]` when there are no models. Each entry is a provider name taken from the model list.
- `id` is `provider/id`. `thinking_levels` is present only for a reasoning model, and is then `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`. `images` is true when the model accepts image input.
- A missing program sets `error` to `pi executable was not found`. No models, with no `error`, means `logged_in` is false.

Errors:

- `500` the saved settings cannot be read
- `500` the status could not be encoded

Events: none.

### GET /v1/claude/status

Auth: admin
Effect: Returns the last Claude detection without waiting. Starts one only when Claude is enabled and no detection has finished. The result names the kind of sign-in, never a credential.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "path": "/usr/local/bin/claude",
  "version": "1.0.80",
  "installed": true,
  "logged_in": true,
  "auth_method": "claude.ai",
  "plan": "Claude Max",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "claude-model",
      "name": "Claude model",
      "description": "General",
      "efforts": ["low", "medium", "high"]
    }
  ],
  "checked_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
  "checking": false,
  "step": "",
  "executable": {"path": "/usr/local/bin/claude", "version": "1.0.80", "auto": true},
  "executables": [{"path": "/usr/local/bin/claude", "version": "1.0.80", "source": "PATH"}]
}
```

- `auth_method` is the sign-in kind Claude reports: `claude.ai` (a subscription), `api_key`, `oauth_token`, a cloud provider's name, or `none`. It is omitted when empty.
- `api_key_source` is omitted above. When present, it names where an API key comes from and never includes the key. `api_provider` is omitted when empty.
- `key_overrides_subscription` is present and true only when a signed-in API key is the active credential, so usage is billed to the API rather than a subscription. Otherwise the field is absent.
- `plan` is the subscription's display name when the model list provided one, otherwise the raw tier. It is omitted when empty.
- On a model, `description` and `efforts` are omitted when empty. `id` is the id or alias Claude accepts. `efforts` is the effort names Claude reports for a model that supports them.
- A missing program sets `error` to `Claude executable was not found`. A sign-in that cannot be read sets `error` to `Could not read Claude's sign-in state: ` plus the failure. Signed out leaves `logged_in` false and `error` omitted.

Errors:

- `500` the saved settings cannot be read
- `500` the status could not be encoded

Events: none.

### POST /v1/claude/status

Auth: admin
Effect: Starts a Claude detection, unless one is already running, and returns the current snapshot immediately. The previous detection stays until the new one finishes; `checking` is then true and `step` starts again at `program`.

```json
  "installed": true,
  "logged_in": false,
  "models": [],
  "checked_at": "2026-10-14T11:00:00Z",
  "checking": true,
  "step": "account",
  "executable": {"path": "/usr/local/bin/claude", "version": "1.0.80", "auto": true},
  "executables": [{"path": "/usr/local/bin/claude", "version": "1.0.80", "source": "PATH"}]
}
```

Errors:

- `500` the saved settings cannot be read
- `500` the status could not be encoded

Events: none.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/agent-usage

Auth: any key
Effect: Returns the Codex, Grok or Claude usage of one conversation, plus that agent's account quota. Any other conversation, including pi, answers with empty parts. Codex account data may wait on a read shared with the account route, up to 20 seconds; a failed read keeps the previous account. Claude account data waits only for the first read since Core started (up to 30 seconds); later an answer older than 60 seconds is served while it is read again, and that read announces `session.agent_usage` for this conversation.

Path: `id` conversation id, `2026-10-14T12-02-00_` plus a UUID. An unknown id or a conversation that does not exist is `404`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "agent": "codex",
  "account": {
    "kind": "chatgpt",
    "plan": "pro",
    "windows": [
      {"id": "5h", "used_percent": 42, "resets_at": "2026-10-14T18:00:00Z", "duration_mins": 300},
      {"id": "weekly", "used_percent": 87, "resets_at": "2026-10-18T00:00:00Z", "duration_mins": 10080}
    ],
    "credits": {"balance": 62500, "has_credits": true, "unlimited": false},
    "updated_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
  },
  "session": {
    "model": "codex-model",
    "turns": 9,
    "input_tokens": 171000,
    "cached_input_tokens": 142500,
    "cache_write_tokens": 800,
    "output_tokens": 13200,
    "reasoning_tokens": 4000,
    "total_tokens": 184200,
    "cost_usd": 0.83,
    "cost_source": "agent_estimate",
    "last_turn": {"total_tokens": 8100, "cost_usd": 0.06},
    "context": {"used_tokens": 62000, "window_tokens": 200000},
    "updated_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

```json
{"agent": null, "account": null, "session": null}
```

- `agent` is `codex`, `grok` or `claude`, or `null` when this conversation is not one of those.
- `session` is `null` until the agent has reported usage. Totals are cumulative as the agent reports them. For a session attached from a terminal they include turns from before the attach. `turns` counts turns finished here for Codex and Claude, and every turn of the session for Grok, because Grok numbers them itself.
- `last_turn` is `null` until a turn has been counted. Its `total_tokens` is that turn's own total. Its `cost_usd` is `null` when that turn's estimate is unknown (the previous estimate was missed, or a thread or session attached from a terminal had usage but no earlier estimate).
- `context` is `null` when no window is known. For Codex, `used_tokens` is the last request's total and `window_tokens` is the model window. For Grok, `used_tokens` is the last turn's input divided by the number of model calls in that turn (exact for one call, lower than the final call when there were several), and `window_tokens` is the context size of the model selected for the conversation, or the session's own figure. Grok's `context` is also `null` when that last turn made no model call. For Claude, `used_tokens` is the last request's input including cache reads and writes, and `window_tokens` is the context window Claude reports for the turn's model.
- `account` is the account object described above. It is `null` for Codex until a read has succeeded. For Grok it is always present: `kind` is `subscription`, `windows` is `[]`, `unavailable_reason` is `not_supported`, and `plan` is the tier from the last Grok detection, omitted when empty. Grok sends no `credits` or `updated_at`.
- A Codex account with `kind` `api_key` has `unavailable_reason` `api_key` and `windows` `[]`. `kind` `unknown` uses `not_signed_in` when nobody is signed in, or `not_supported` for any other account type.
- Claude's account is `null` until a read has succeeded (also while Claude is disabled). A subscription sign-in has `kind` `subscription` and `plan` (such as `max`); its `windows` are the plan limits, or `[]` with `unavailable_reason` `not_supported` when Claude reported none. An API key is `kind` `api_key` with `unavailable_reason` `api_key`. Signed out is `kind` `unknown` with `not_signed_in`; another sign-in (a cloud provider) is `unknown` with `not_supported`. `credits` is present only when Claude's extra usage is enabled: `has_credits` is true, `balance` is what is left of the monthly limit, or `null` when unknown, and `unlimited` is true when there is no monthly limit.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `500` a binding cannot be read
- `500` cannot read agent usage

Events: none.

### GET /v1/local-agents/{agent}/account-usage

Auth: any key
Effect: Returns the same account object as the conversation usage route, before a conversation exists. `codex` may wait on the shared read (20 seconds, at most once a minute; a failed read keeps the last account). `grok` does not start Grok; it answers from the last detection. `claude` shares the conversation route's cache and waits only for the first read.

Path: `agent` is `codex`, `grok` or `claude`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "kind": "chatgpt",
  "plan": "pro",
  "windows": [
    {"id": "5h", "used_percent": 42, "resets_at": "2026-10-14T18:00:00Z", "duration_mins": 300}
  ],
  "credits": {"balance": 62500, "has_credits": true, "unlimited": false},
  "updated_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
}
```

```json
null
```

- Codex and Claude are `null` until a read has succeeded. The fields are the account object on `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/agent-usage`.
- Grok is never `null`:

```json
{"kind": "subscription", "windows": [], "unavailable_reason": "not_supported"}
```

`plan` is added when the last Grok detection reported a tier.

Errors:

- `404` unknown external agent

`pi`, `claude` and any other name use this same `404`.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/local-agents/{agent}/terminal-sessions

Auth: any key (admin for an agent that does not allow non-administrators)
Effect: Lists sessions the agent started on this computer outside Core, newest first, 30 a page. Codex includes threads from the CLI, an editor extension, a one-shot run and the desktop app, and leaves subagent threads out. Grok includes its stored sessions. Claude Code includes every session it saved on this computer (read from its own session files; subagent transcripts and sessions without a prompt or a reply are left out). A successful page may be reused for 15 seconds; whether a session is open, its directory is missing, or it is already attached is computed on every response. The request waits for the agent, up to 20 seconds.

Path: `agent` is `codex`, `grok` or `claude`. `pi` is known but unsupported.

Query: `scope` is `dir` or `all`. Omitted, it is `all`, or `dir` when `cwd` is present. `cwd` is the directory for `scope=dir` and must be absolute; it is ignored for `all`. `cursor` is the `next_cursor` of the previous page, omitted for the first page. Do not parse it.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "agent": "grok",
      "id": "thread-7c2e9a",
      "title": "Fix the login form",
      "cwd": "/home/dev/app",
      "updated_at": "2026-10-14T11:40:00Z",
      "preview": "The login form rejects valid passwords",
      "model": "grok-model",
      "sandbox": "workspace",
      "message_count": 12,
      "in_use": false,
      "cwd_missing": false,
      "attached_conversation_id": "2026-10-13T09-15-22_018f3a2b-7c4e-7a1b-8d2e-9a0b1c2d3e4f"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "page-2"
}
```

- `sessions` is `[]` when there is nothing on this page. `next_cursor` is omitted on the last page. Rows Core started itself are removed, so a page can be shorter than 30 while `next_cursor` is still set. Keep paging until it is absent.
- `id` is the agent's own session id. `cwd` is the agent's own directory string and must be sent back unchanged to attach. `title` may be `""`. Codex and Claude titles are one line and at most 100 characters, using the thread name (Claude: the name given with `/rename`, else Claude's generated title) or else the start of its first message. Grok titles are as Grok reports them.
- `updated_at` is UTC RFC3339 for Codex and Claude (for Claude, when its session file was last written). For Grok it is the timestamp string Grok reported.
- `preview` is the start of the first prompt on one line, at most 120 characters, ending with `…` when cut. It is omitted when empty.
- `model` is omitted when empty. `sandbox` and `message_count` are filled for Grok when it has a summary, and omitted for Codex (Codex does not report them on this list). Claude has no sandbox; its `model` is the full model ID of the last reply (such as `claude-opus-5-5`) and `message_count` counts prompts and replies with text. `message_count` is also omitted when 0.
- `in_use` is true when a terminal has the session open. `cwd_missing` is true when `cwd` is not a directory on the Core host. `attached_conversation_id` is set when this session was attached and that conversation still exists. A session Core started stays hidden after its conversation is deleted. An attached terminal session is listed again after its conversation is deleted, and can be attached again.

Errors:

- `400` scope must be dir or all
- `400` cwd must be an absolute directory on the Core host
- `400` Terminal sessions are not supported for pi yet
- `400` Codex is disabled in Settings → External agents
- `400` Grok is disabled in Settings → External agents
- `400` Claude is disabled in Settings → External agents
- `400` Codex executable was not found
- `400` Grok executable was not found
- `400` invalid cursor
- `403` Ask an administrator to turn on "Allow non-administrators" for Codex in Settings → External agents.
- `404` unknown external agent
- `500` the agent could not list sessions, or the bindings could not be read

The `403` names the agent (`Codex`, `Grok` or `Claude`). `pi` is rejected with the unsupported `400` before that check. `invalid cursor` is Claude's answer to a cursor it did not issue. The disabled and missing-program `400` name whichever agent was asked.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/local-agents/{agent}/terminal-sessions/{external_id}/attach

Auth: any key (admin for an agent that does not allow non-administrators)
Effect: Binds a terminal session to a conversation and copies its history into the transcript. A new conversation is created when this session is not already attached. Attaching it again returns the conversation it already has; if that import never finished, the history is imported again and rows already written are not repeated. A failed create removes the new conversation. The call waits for the import and stops after 5 minutes.

Path: `agent` is `codex`, `grok` or `claude`. `external_id` is the `id` from the list. A blank id is rejected.

Request:

```json
{"cwd": "/home/dev/app", "project_id": "018f3a2b-7c4e-7a1b-8d2e-9a0b1c2d3e4f"}
```

- `cwd` is required. It must be absolute and must be the listed `cwd` in that exact spelling, with nothing added. The body is at most 16384 bytes. Extra fields are ignored.
- `project_id` is optional, a project UUID. When set, the conversation joins that project and `cwd` must sit inside one of its directories. When omitted, the conversation's workspace is `cwd` itself.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-02-00_018f3a2b-7c4e-7a1b-8d2e-9a0b1c2d3e4f",
  "existing": false
}
```

- `session_id` is the conversation. `existing` is false when this call created it, and true when the session was already attached to a conversation that still exists.
- Imported transcript rows carry `importedFrom` `terminal`. They are history the agent already has, so they are not sent again. A Codex thread whose sandbox is neither `read-only` nor `workspace-write` continues under the saved Codex sandbox. A Claude session continues under the saved Claude permission mode and Gyres approvals, whatever permission mode it ran with in the terminal; its origin has no `sandbox`.
- The conversation's title is set from the session when it has one and the conversation has none. Codex keeps the thread's model and effort when that model is offered; an effort the model does not offer is dropped, and a model that is not offered is replaced by the first offered model with the effort cleared. With no model list yet, both are kept. Grok keeps the session's model when it has one, and otherwise uses the first model Grok offers. Claude maps the session's full model ID to the offered model of the same ID or family (`claude-opus-5-5` becomes `opus`), else the first offered model; effort follows the Codex rule.

Errors:

- `400` cwd must be the session's directory as listed
- `400` missing session id
- `400` cwd must be the session's directory exactly as listed
- `400` Terminal sessions are not supported for pi yet
- `400` Codex is disabled in Settings → External agents
- `400` Grok is disabled in Settings → External agents
- `400` Claude is disabled in Settings → External agents
- `400` Codex executable was not found
- `400` Grok executable was not found
- `400` project not found
- `400` current directory must be inside a project directory
- `400` invalid project cwd
- `400` create the project library, or create the conversation directory, when that directory cannot be created
- `403` Ask an administrator to turn on "Allow non-administrators" for Codex in Settings → External agents.
- `404` unknown external agent
- `404` Claude session file not found
- `404` invalid Claude session ID
- `409` This Codex session already belongs to a Gyres conversation
- `409` This session is open in a terminal. Exit it there first, then attach it.
- `409` The session's directory no longer exists on the Core host
- `409` turn already running
- `500` the history could not be imported, or the conversation could not be created

`invalid project cwd` includes the path and the reason. The "already belongs" `409` names the agent (`Codex`, `Grok` or `Claude`) and is a session Core itself started. `turn already running` also covers a conversation that cannot accept the import right now. The `403` names the agent, as on the list route.

Events: `sessions.changed`, `session.messages`, `session.settings`

A new conversation announces `sessions.changed`. Imported rows announce `session.messages`. Saving a model announces `session.settings`, and setting a title announces `sessions.changed` again. An already imported session announces nothing. A failed create announces `sessions.changed` as the new conversation is removed.


<!-- file: http/approvals.md -->

# Tool approvals

A frontend uses these routes to show tool calls that are waiting for the owner, to approve or reject them, and to read or change the policy and the remembered grants. Core keeps the decision. Closing the page does not approve, reject or cancel a waiting request, and any client with a key can decide it. A call that is read-only, the `subagent` tool, or one of these actions never appears here: `memory` `read`, `schedule` `list` or `report`, `schedule_manage` `list`, `skill_manage` `list` or `read`, `computer_use` `capture`, `list_apps`, `list_windows` or `wait`. The managed browser does not ask. A call that a grant or the policy already allows runs without a new request. The same operation rejected or denied earlier in that run does not ask again.

A failed request uses the JSON error body: `error` is the message named below.

Request `id` and grant `id` are 32 lowercase hex characters. Timestamps are UTC.

`config.mode` is the attended policy: `ask`, `edit` or `allow`. The initial value is `ask`. `config.unattended` is the policy for a call with `unattended` true (a scheduled run), used instead of `mode`: `deny`, `wait` or `allow`. The initial value is `deny`.

- `ask` asks, unless a grant covers the call.
- `edit` does the same, and also allows `write` and `edit` when the target file is inside the conversation's working directory or a workspace root. It does not by itself allow other tools.
- `allow` allows the attended call without asking.
- Unattended `deny` stores the request as `denied` and does not run the call. `reason` is `unattended policy denies operations requiring approval`.
- Unattended `wait` leaves the request `pending` until a client decides it.
- Unattended `allow` runs the unattended call without a request.

A request with `once_only` true is never covered by a mode, a grant or unattended `allow`. An unattended one is denied under every unattended policy, and `reason` is `unattended runs refuse operations only a person may approve; it would have hit:` followed by a newline and `resource`. This is `exec_command` when it would signal a process Core did not start. Clipboard and recording ask unless a grant covers them; `mode` and unattended `allow` do not. An ordinary app asks unless the owner's app mode already allows it. An app reserved to the Core host never creates a request. A blocked app, or an app outside an allow list, fails without a request. An external agent, a plugin tool, and an MCP tool other than the managed browser follow `ask`, `edit` and `allow` like any other call.

`session_modes` overrides `mode` per conversation. A missing entry inherits `config.mode`. A request with `policy_session` uses the mode of that parent conversation instead of its own. A child conversation's own entry cannot be set.

A grant with `scope` `global` omits `session_id` and applies in every conversation. A grant with `scope` `session` includes `session_id` and applies to that conversation and to a request whose `policy_session` is that same id. `tool_wide` true matches the same `tool` and the same `tool_identity` (both empty still matches) and does not depend on `resource`. Otherwise the grant matches the same `tool` and the same `key` only. Grants are also created outside a card, for example a global tool grant made on the Core host; they appear in this list and are revoked here. `key` is an opaque match string, not a credential. Request objects do not include it.

`status` on a request is `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `denied`, `expired` or `cancelled`. `scope` on an approved request is `once`, `session` or `global`. `finished_at` is set once the request leaves `pending`. A restart stores a still-waiting request as `expired` with `reason` `Core restarted; this operation was not replayed`.

Changes publish `approvals.changed` on `GET /v1/events`, with no conversation id. One request can publish it more than once. Refetch `GET /v1/approvals`. Submitting a policy or a mode that is already stored publishes nothing.

### GET /v1/approvals

Auth: any key
Effect: Returns the policy, the per-conversation modes, every grant, the waiting requests, and one page of decision history.

Query: `session_id` (string, optional) keeps only requests whose `session_id` equals this conversation. It does not filter `pending`, `pending_requests`, grants or `session_modes`. An empty value does not filter. `offset` (int, optional) is the start of the history page. A missing value, or a value that is not an integer, counts as 0. A negative value counts as 0. A value past the filtered history counts as the end of it. The page holds at most 100 requests. There is no page-size parameter.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "next_offset": 1,
  "pending": 1,
  "pending_requests": [
    {
      "tool_wide": true,
      "id": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90",
      "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-00-00_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef",
      "run_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "tool_call_id": "call_01",
      "tool": "exec_command",
      "resource": "{\"command\":\"printf hello\"}",
      "input": {"command": "printf hello"},
      "cwd": "/work/demo",
      "unattended": false,
      "status": "pending",
      "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "requests": [
    {
      "tool_wide": true,
      "id": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90",
      "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-00-00_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef",
      "run_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "tool_call_id": "call_01",
      "tool": "exec_command",
      "resource": "{\"command\":\"printf hello\"}",
      "input": {"command": "printf hello"},
      "cwd": "/work/demo",
      "unattended": false,
      "status": "pending",
      "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "state": {
    "config": {"mode": "ask", "unattended": "deny"},
    "grants": [
      {
        "tool_wide": true,
        "cwd": "/work/demo",
        "id": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
        "key": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
        "tool": "exec_command",
        "resource": "{\"command\":\"printf hello\"}",
        "scope": "session",
        "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-00-00_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef",
        "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "session_modes": {
      "2026-10-14T12-00-00_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef": "edit"
    }
  },
  "total": 1
}
```

- `state.config` is the policy above. `state.grants` is every grant, in stored order, or `[]`. `state.session_modes` maps a conversation id to `ask`, `edit` or `allow`, or `{}`.
- `requests` is the history page, newest `created_at` first, every `status`, after the `session_id` filter. `total` is the filtered count before paging. `next_offset` is the index just after this page; it equals `total` when this page reaches the end.
- `pending` is the number of requests with `status` `pending`, across every conversation. `pending_requests` is those requests, newest first, not paged and not filtered. A waiting request is also in `requests` when the filter and the page include it.
- Request fields that are present when set: `tool_identity` (string), `tool_wide` (true), `policy_session` (parent conversation id), `tool_label` (text to show), `once_only` (true), `scope`, `reason`, `resolver`, `finished_at`. They are omitted when empty. `unattended` false is still present.
- `tool` is the tool name.
