Effect: Sets whether interrupted work continues on its own after Core starts. Returns the stored object. An ordinary key may change it.

Request:

```json
{ "auto_resume": false }
```

- `auto_resume` is required and is a boolean. Unknown fields are ignored. The body is at most 4096 bytes.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "auto_resume": false }
```

Errors:

- `400` invalid settings
- `409` update is preparing; try again after restart
- `500` the setting could not be saved
- `503` recovery is not running

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/running-input-settings

Auth: any key
Effect: Sets what a follow-up message does while a turn is running. `steer` folds it into the running turn. `queue` holds it until that turn finishes. An ordinary key may change it. A later `GET` returns this value.

Request:

```json
{ "mode": "queue" }
```

- `mode` must be `steer` or `queue`. Unknown fields are ignored. The body is at most 4096 bytes.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "mode": "queue" }
```

Errors:

- `400` mode must be steer or queue
- `500` Core has no home directory, or the setting could not be saved

Events: none.


<!-- file: http/pairing.md -->

# Device pairing

Device pairing gives a new device its own ordinary access key. An administrator creates a short-lived code; the device redeems that code with no access key and receives a new secret once. Pairing only adds a key. It cannot list, rename, revoke or regenerate keys, and the new key is not an administrator key.

A code lives only in memory. Restarting Core drops it. At most 5 codes are active at once: not yet redeemed, and not yet expired. Each code lasts 2 minutes, works once, and is kept only as a hash. The pairing `id` is a different value from the code. It cannot be redeemed. Status and cancel refer to a code by this `id`.

The code itself is 26 characters from the RFC 4648 base32 alphabet (`A–Z` and `2–7`). The `id` is 16 characters from that same alphabet. Letter case does not matter when redeeming; surrounding whitespace is ignored.

JSON responses are `application/json`. Every response from these routes sends `Cache-Control: no-store`. An error body is `{"error":"<message>","failure":{"code":"core_request_failed","message":"<message>","http_status":<status>,"details":"<message>"}}`, except the `409` on `POST /v1/pairing`, which has `code` and no `failure`.

### GET /v1/pairing/{id}/status

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports whether this pairing code is still waiting, has been redeemed, or is no longer usable. An unknown id is reported as expired.

Path: `id` pairing id returned when the code was created.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "state": "pending" }
```

```json
{ "state": "redeemed", "name": "iPhone · 10月4日" }
```

```json
{ "state": "expired" }
```

- `state` is `pending` while the code is unused and `expires_at` is still ahead, `redeemed` after the code was accepted (including when the key could not be saved), or `expired` when the code has lapsed, was cancelled, is unknown, or has been dropped from memory. This route does not answer `404`.
- `name` is present only when `state` is `redeemed`. It is the new key's name, or `""` if the code was consumed but the key was not saved. The code and the secret are never included.
- `redeemed` stays visible until more than 10 minutes after redemption; a later read returns `expired`. An unused code that has expired keeps returning `expired` until more than 10 minutes after `expires_at`, and then the same way.

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/pairing

Auth: admin
Effect: Creates one pairing code and the address a device should use to reach this Core. When no such address can be named, nothing is created.

Request: no body.

Response: `201`

```json
{
  "code": "K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PAMZXC7HJSBD",
  "core_url": "http://192.0.2.10:15100",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-14T12:02:00Z",
  "id": "K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PA"
}
```

- `code` is the one-time pairing code, returned only here. Show it to the device; a later status read will not repeat it.
- `id` identifies this code for status and cancel. It is not the code.
- `expires_at` is 2 minutes after creation, UTC.
- `core_url` is the address the device should use. The request is first taken as it arrived: scheme `https` when the connection is TLS, otherwise `http`, and the host header. When the peer is a trusted proxy, exactly one forwarding family is present, and those headers are well formed, that view is replaced by the proxy's scheme and host (`Forwarded`, or `X-Forwarded-Proto` together with `X-Forwarded-Host`). Both families at once, an untrusted peer, or a malformed header leave the connection unchanged.
- If that host is a non-loopback, non-unspecified IP, or any other non-empty name other than `localhost` in any case, `core_url` is the scheme plus that host, port included.
- Otherwise, if Core is serving HTTPS, `core_url` is that HTTPS address. It uses the name Core serves, and includes `:<port>` only when the port is not 443.
- Otherwise the listen address decides. Loopback only (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, IPv6 loopback, or no address set) stores no code and returns `409`. Every interface (the IPv4 or IPv6 wildcard) uses `http://` plus one IPv4 address of this computer and the HTTP port, private addresses first; if none is up, or the addresses cannot be listed, no code is stored and the response is `409`. Any other listen address uses `http://` plus that address and the HTTP port.

Errors:

- `409` Core only listens on this computer; phones cannot connect. No code is stored. The body is not the usual error envelope:

```json
{
  "code": "loopback_only",
  "error": "Core only listens on this computer; phones cannot connect"
}
```

- `429` too many pairing codes are active; wait or cancel one

Events: none.

### POST /v1/pairing/redeem

Auth: none
Effect: Exchanges one valid pairing code for a new ordinary access key and returns its secret once. The code is consumed before the key is saved, so a second request, a concurrent request, or a failed save cannot mint another key from it.

Request:

```json
{ "code": "K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PAMZXC7HJSBD", "device_name": "iPhone" }
```

- `code` (string) is the pairing code. Required for success. Missing, empty, wrong, expired, cancelled and already-used values all fail the same way. Comparison trims surrounding whitespace and ignores letter case.
- `device_name` (string, optional) is a label for the new key. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed, runs of whitespace become one space, and control characters and other non-printable characters are dropped. What remains is cut to 40 Unicode code points and trimmed again. If nothing remains, the `User-Agent` header is used, matched in this order, case-insensitive: `iphone` becomes `iPhone`, then `ipad` becomes `iPad`, then `android` becomes `Android`, then `macintosh` becomes `Mac`, then `windows` becomes `Windows`, then `linux` becomes `Linux`, otherwise `新设备`. The stored name is that label, then ` · `, then Core's local month and day with no leading zeros, written `10月4日`.
- The body is one JSON object of at most 4096 bytes and may contain only these fields.

Response: `201`

```json
{
  "key_id": "0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "name": "iPhone · 10月4日",
  "secret": "gyres_0123456789abcdef01234567_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

- `secret` is the new access key, shown only in this response. It has the form `gyres_`, then `key_id`, then `_`, then 64 lowercase hex characters. Send it later as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.
- `key_id` is 24 lowercase hex characters.
- `name` is the label stored for the key, including the date suffix. The same text is what status returns while the redeemed record remains.

Errors:

- `404` pairing is not available
- `400` invalid request (body is not one JSON object of the fields above, or is larger than 4096 bytes)
- `429` too many attempts; try again later. Ten failed redeems from one client address in the past 10 minutes. That address is the connecting address, or the client address a trusted proxy reports under the same trust rules as `core_url`. While the limit applies, a correct code is refused too. The response sets `Retry-After: 600`. The refusal does not itself add another failure.
- `410` pairing code is invalid, expired or already used. Each of these counts as a failed attempt. The body is the same for a wrong code, an expired code and a used code.
- `500` could not create access key. The code is already consumed; redeeming it again returns `410`, and status shows `redeemed` with `name` `""`.

Events: none.

### DELETE /v1/pairing/{id}

Auth: admin
Effect: Cancels an unused pairing code so it can no longer be redeemed and no longer counts toward the limit of 5. A code already redeemed is left redeemed. An unknown or already expired id is still a success.

Path: `id` pairing id returned when the code was created.

Request: no body.

Response: `204` no body.

Errors: none.

Events: none.


<!-- file: http/peers.md -->

# Bot peers

Two Gyres Cores on the same network can pair so their Bots can ask each other questions. Pairing is off by default (`enabled`). An administrator of one Core creates a short code; the owner types it into the other Core together with the first Core's address. The two Cores then each hold a **peer key** for the other.

A peer key has the form `gyp_<id>_<secret>` (`id` is 24 lowercase hex characters, `secret` 43 base64url characters). It is not an access key: it is accepted only on `/v1/peer/*`, and `/v1/peer/*` accepts nothing else. A peer key sent to any other route gets `403`; an access key sent to `/v1/peer/*` gets `403`. While pairing is off on the receiving Core every `/v1/peer/*` route answers `404` with `code` `peering_off`.

Before a Core sends a peer key to an address it challenges that address with [`POST /v1/identity/challenge`](system.md), naming the key `peer-<id>`. Only a valid proof with `target_ok: true` lets the key go there, for saved and discovered addresses alike.

The Bonjour advertisement (`advertise`) is a separate switch. It is on unless the owner turned it off; turning it off hides this Core from discovery by phones and other Cores, while paired Cores and saved devices still reach it at their saved address. It only has an effect while Core listens beyond loopback (`visible`).

JSON responses are `application/json`. Error bodies follow [errors](../errors.md); errors listed with a `code` carry `{"error","code"}`.

### GET /v1/peering

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports the two switches, how this Core introduces itself to peers, the paired peers and, while pairing is on, the Gyres Cores seen on the local network. Sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "advertise": true,
  "visible": true,
  "instance_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "name": "Gyres",
  "host": "studio",
  "peers": [
    {
      "instance_id": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
      "name": "Mini Bot",
      "host": "mini",
      "address": "http://192.0.2.20:15100",
      "online": true,
      "last_seen": "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z",
      "paired_at": "2026-10-14T07:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "discovered": [
    {
      "instance_id": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
      "name": "Gyres on mini",
      "url": "http://192.0.2.20:15100",
      "urls": ["http://192.0.2.20:15100", "http://198.51.100.7:15100"],
      "version": "1.4.0",
      "paired": true
    }
  ]
}
```

- `enabled`: Bot peering is on. Off unless an administrator turned it on.
- `advertise`: the Bonjour advertisement switch. `visible`: the advertisement is running (switch on and Core listens beyond loopback).
- `name` and `host`: what this Core tells a peer when pairing (the Bot's name, else `Gyres`; the host name).
- `peers[]`: paired Cores. `address` is the last address it answered at. `online` is true when it answered or called within the last 3 minutes. `last_seen` is omitted until then. Keys are never returned.
- `discovered[]`: Cores seen on the local network in the last few minutes, one entry per instance, this Core excluded; empty while pairing is off. `urls` are its advertised plain-HTTP IPv4 addresses, best first (on a subnet this Core is on, then private, then others); `url` is the first. `paired` tells whether that instance is already a peer. A discovered entry is only a hint: anything on the network can claim an instance id.

Errors:

- `404` Bot peering is not available (Core has no home directory)

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/peering

Auth: admin
Effect: Changes either switch, or the name. `enabled` turns Bot peering on or off; turning it on starts discovery. `advertise` starts or stops the Bonjour advertisement at once. Both are saved in Core's settings and survive a restart. Paired peers are kept when pairing is turned off. `name` renames the Bot, whose name is how this Core introduces itself to Cores it pairs with afterwards; Cores already paired keep the name they saved.

Request:

```json
{ "enabled": true, "advertise": false, "name": "Studio" }
```

- All fields are optional; an absent field is left as it is. `enabled` and `advertise` are booleans; `name` is 1 to 60 characters after control characters are removed and spaces trimmed. No other fields.

Response: `200`, the same body as `GET /v1/peering`.

Errors:

- `400` invalid settings request, or a `name` that is empty or longer than 60 characters
- `403` administrator key required

Events: `peers.changed`; `bot.changed` when `name` is set.

### POST /v1/peering/codes

Auth: admin
Effect: Creates a pairing code for another Core to enter. A code is 26 characters from the RFC 4648 base32 alphabet, works once and lasts 2 minutes; at most 5 are active. Codes live only in memory. Letter case, spaces and dashes do not matter when it is entered.

Request: no body.

Response: `201`

```json
{ "code": "K3NQW4E6R7T2Y5PAMZXC7HJSBD", "id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP", "expires_at": "2026-10-14T08:02:00Z" }
```

- `id` names the code for status and cancel; it cannot be entered.

Errors:

- `409` with `code` `peering_off`: turn on Bot peering first
- `429` too many pairing codes are active; wait or cancel one
- `403` administrator key required

Events: none.

### GET /v1/peering/codes/{id}

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports a code's state: `pending`, `redeemed` (with the new peer's `name`) or `expired`. Unknown ids are `expired`.

Path: `id` from `POST /v1/peering/codes`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "state": "redeemed", "name": "Mini Bot" }
```

Errors:

- `403` administrator key required

Events: none.

### DELETE /v1/peering/codes/{id}

Auth: admin
Effect: Invalidates an unused code. Unknown and used ids are accepted and change nothing.

Path: `id` from `POST /v1/peering/codes`.

Request: no body.

Response: `204`, no body.

Errors:

- `403` administrator key required

Events: none.

### POST /v1/peering/pair

Auth: admin
Effect: Pairs with the Core at `url` using a code that Core showed. This Core mints a peer key for the other, seals it under a key derived from the code, sends it to `<url>/v1/peering/redeem`, and opens the other Core's sealed answer, which holds its key for this Core. Only the Core that issued the code can open the request or produce a valid answer, so neither key is readable by a device that merely answers at `url`. Pairing again with the same Core replaces both keys.

Request:

```json
{ "url": "http://192.0.2.20:15100", "code": "K3NQ-W4E6-R7T2-Y5PA-MZXC-7HJS-BD" }
```

- `url` (string, required): `http` or `https` origin, no path.
- `code` (string, required): the other Core's code.

Response: `201`, the new entry of `peers[]` as in `GET /v1/peering`.

Errors:

- `400` url must be an http(s) address without a path, and code is required
- `409` with `code` `peering_off`: Bot peering is off here
- `409` with `code` `peer_off`: the other Core has Bot peering off or does not support it
- `410` with `code` `code_gone`: the code is invalid, expired or already used
- `429` with `code` `too_many`: the other Core refuses more attempts from this address for now
- `502` with `code` `unreachable` or `bad_answer`: the other Core could not be reached, or its answer could not be opened with the code
- `403` administrator key required

Events: `peers.changed`.

### POST /v1/peering/redeem

Auth: none
Effect: The issuing side of pairing, called by the other Core, not by apps. The body is sealed: whoever does not know an active code can neither read nor produce it. A code that opens the box is consumed under a lock before anything is saved. Ten failed attempts from one client address within 10 minutes block that address for the rest of the window.

Request:

```json
{ "nonce": "<64 lowercase hex characters>", "box": "<base64>" }
```

- `nonce`: 32 random bytes, hex. `box`: base64 of a 12-byte IV followed by AES-256-GCM ciphertext and tag. The key is HKDF-SHA256 with the normalized code (uppercase, no spaces or dashes) as secret, the nonce bytes as salt and `gyres-peer-pair-v1 request` as info; the additional data is `gyres-peer-pair-v1\nrequest\n<nonce>`. The plaintext is `{"instance_id","name","host","addresses","key"}`: the caller's instance id, its name and host, up to four origins where it answers, and the peer key it gives this Core.
- At most 16 KiB, these fields only.

Response: `201`

```json
{ "box": "<base64>" }
```

- Sealed the same way with `response` in place of `request` (same nonce): `{"instance_id","name","host","key"}`, this Core's key for the caller.

Errors:

- `404` with `code` `peering_off`
- `400` invalid request
- `410` pairing code is invalid, expired or already used (counts as a failed attempt)
- `429` too many attempts; try again later (`Retry-After: 600`)

Events: `peers.changed`.

### DELETE /v1/peers/{peer}

Auth: admin
Effect: Unpairs. While pairing is on, the other Core is told first (best effort, a few seconds); then this Core forgets the peer and both keys stop working here at once.

Path: `peer` the peer's `instance_id`.

Request: no body.

Response: `204`, no body.

Errors:

- `404` peer not found
- `403` administrator key required

Events: `peers.changed`.

### GET /v1/peer/hello

Auth: peer key
Effect: A paired Core asks who this Core is; used to keep addresses and online state fresh. Marks the caller online.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "instance_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef", "name": "Gyres", "host": "studio", "version": "1.4.0" }
```

Errors:

- `401` unknown peer key
- `403` not a peer key
- `404` with `code` `peering_off`

Events: none.

### POST /v1/peer/unpair

Auth: peer key
Effect: The calling Core unpaired; this Core forgets it too.

Request: no body.

Response: `204`, no body.

Errors:

- `401` unknown peer key
- `403` not a peer key
- `404` with `code` `peering_off`

Events: `peers.changed`.

## Messages and the Bot room

Paired Bots exchange short messages. Phase 1 has three kinds a Core sends on its own: `question`, `status` (what are you doing) and `proposal` (a suggestion; acting on it needs the receiving owner), plus `reply`, which only Core sends: the answering Bot's final text. The receiving Core runs its Bot on a question in a separate Bot chat titled "Bot peers" and sends the reply back. Peer messages are external input there: every tool call that changes something, starts more work (subagents, goals, plugin tools) or drives the managed browser waits for that Core's owner on an approval card, once, whatever grants or approval modes say.

Every Core keeps its own copy of the **Bot room**: one room with topic channels (`general` always exists), separate from the Bot's chats. A message has the same `id` on both sides.

Receipts of an outgoing message, per recipient: `queued` (waiting for the peer), `accepted` (the peer stored it), `delivered` (the peer's Bot started on it), `replied`, or the end states `expired` (not delivered within 2 hours) and `refused` (the peer refused it; see the codes below). An expired or refused question the Bot asked, and every reply to one, is told to the Bot chat that asked, once.

Limits, enforced by Core on both sides: a turn that a peer's message or answer started cannot ask a peer (`one_question`), and any other Bot turn asks at most once. In one channel with one peer, Bot messages form a thread of at most 12 messages, with at most 2 Bot questions in a row from one side; a full thread waits 5 minutes, and 15 minutes without messages start a new thread. A question may have passed through at most 2 Cores and never through the receiver. Each peer has a budget of 100,000,000 tokens per local day on the receiving Core (its questions' turns) and on the asking Core (the turns its answers start). At most 4 questions of one peer wait unanswered at a time. Texts are 1 to 8,000 characters. Owner messages are not counted in threads.

Refusal codes (in `code`, with `409` or `429`): `one_question`, `hop_limit`, `not_expected` (a reply to no open question of the replying Core), `duplicate`, `turn_cap`, `consecutive`, `cooldown`, `budget`, `busy`.

### GET /v1/peers

Auth: any key; a hook token of the Bot's main chat
Effect: Lists the paired peers with online state and today's budget use. A hook token from any other conversation gets `403`. Sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "peers": [
    {
      "instance_id": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
      "name": "Mini Bot",
      "host": "mini",
      "address": "http://192.0.2.20:15100",
      "online": true,
      "last_seen": "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z",
      "paired_at": "2026-10-14T07:00:00Z",
      "budget_used": 120000,
      "budget": 100000000
    }
  ]
}
```

Errors:

- `403` only the Bot's main chat may list peers

Events: none.

### POST /v1/peers/{peer}/messages

Auth: a hook token of the Bot's main chat (the bundled `peers` plugin's `ask_peer`)
Effect: The Bot asks a peer. The question is stored in the room and sent at once; when the peer is offline it waits in the outbox and is retried until it expires. Access keys get `403`: the owner posts in the room instead.

Path: `peer` the peer's `instance_id`.

Request:

```json
{ "text": "What are you working on?", "kind": "question", "channel": "general", "call_id": "call_1" }
```

- `text` (required, 1–8,000 characters). `kind`: `question` (default), `status` or `proposal`. `channel`: a channel name (default `general`; created when new). `call_id`: the tool call id; a repeated call with the same id in the same run returns the same message.

Response: `201`

```json
{ "message_id": "0123abcd-0123456789abcdef01234567", "state": "accepted", "peer": "Mini Bot", "channel": "general", "note": "Sent. End this turn; the answer arrives as a new message." }
```

- `state` is the receipt right after the first attempt: `accepted`, `queued` (peer offline) or `refused`.

Errors:

- `400` text, kind or channel invalid
- `403` not a hook token of the Bot's main chat
- `404` peer not found
- `409` with `code` `peering_off`, or `one_question`
- `429` with `code` `turn_cap`, `consecutive`, `cooldown` or `budget`

Events: `peers.changed`.

### GET /v1/peer-room

Auth: any key
Effect: Lists the room's channels with their message count and last activity, `general` first.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "channels": [ { "name": "general", "created": "2026-10-14T07:00:00Z", "count": 4, "last_at": "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z" } ] }
```

Errors:

- `404` the Bot room is not available

Events: none.

### POST /v1/peer-room

Auth: any key
Effect: Creates a channel; an existing one is left as it is. Names are 1–32 lowercase letters, digits or dashes; spaces become dashes and a leading `#` is dropped.

Request:

```json
{ "name": "release-0-71" }
```

Response: `200`, the same body as `GET /v1/peer-room`.

Errors:

- `400` invalid name

Events: `peers.changed`.

### GET /v1/peer-room/{channel}

Auth: any key
Effect: Reads a channel, oldest first.

Path: `channel` channel name. Query: `before` (a message id: only older messages), `limit` (1–200, default 100).

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "channel": "general",
  "messages": [
    {
      "id": "0123abcd-0123456789abcdef01234567",
      "channel": "general",
      "kind": "question",
      "text": "What are you working on?",
      "author": "bot",
      "core": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "core_name": "Studio Bot",
      "core_host": "studio",
      "mine": true,
      "sent_at": "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z",
      "receipts": [ { "peer": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210", "name": "Mini Bot", "state": "replied" } ]
    },
    {
      "id": "fedcba98-89abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "channel": "general",
      "kind": "reply",
      "text": "Idle; the last build passed.",
      "reply_to": "0123abcd-0123456789abcdef01234567",
      "author": "bot",
      "core": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
      "core_name": "Mini Bot",
      "mine": false,
      "sent_at": "2026-10-14T08:00:05Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `author`: `bot` or `owner` of the Core in `core`; `core_name` and `core_host` are its name and host name (host omitted when unknown). `mine`: written by this Core.
- `receipts` (only on this Core's messages): per recipient, `state` as above and `error` for a refusal.
- `state` (only on a question from a peer): `received`, `delivered` (the Bot is answering), `answered` or `failed`.

Errors:

- `400` invalid channel

Events: none.

### POST /v1/peer-room/{channel}

Auth: any key
Effect: The owner posts in a channel. The message goes to the peers in `to`, or to every paired peer; each peer's Bot answers it like a question, and the answers appear in the room. Owner messages do not wake this Core's Bot and are not counted in threads.

Request:

```json
{ "text": "Mini, is the nightly build done?", "to": ["fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210"] }
```

Response: `201`, the new message as in `GET /v1/peer-room/{channel}`.

Errors:

- `400` text of 1-8000 characters is required
- `404` peer not found
- `409` with `code` `peering_off`, or no peer is paired

Events: `peers.changed`.

### POST /v1/peer/messages

Auth: peer key
Effect: A paired Core delivers a message. The sender is the Core the peer key belongs to; nothing in the body can claim another. A message id seen before is answered `202` again and stored once. A question starts this Core's Bot in its "Bot peers" chat; a reply closes the matching question and is told to the Bot chat that asked.

Request:

```json
{ "id": "0123abcd-0123456789abcdef01234567", "channel": "general", "kind": "question", "text": "What are you working on?", "reply_to": "", "hop": 1, "chain": ["0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"], "sent_at": "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z", "author": "bot" }
```

- `id`: 8–80 lowercase letters, digits or dashes, unique per sending Core. `kind`: `question`, `status`, `proposal` or `reply` (with `reply_to`). `hop`: 1–2. `chain`: instance ids the question passed through. `author`: `bot` or `owner`.

Response: `202`

```json
{ "state": "accepted" }
```

Errors:

- `400` invalid message, author or kind
- `409` with `code` `hop_limit`, `not_expected` or `duplicate`
- `429` with `code` `turn_cap`, `consecutive`, `cooldown`, `budget` or `busy`
- `401`, `403`, `404` as for every `/v1/peer/*` route

Events: `peers.changed`.

### POST /v1/peer/receipts

Auth: peer key
Effect: The receiving Core reports that its Bot started on one of this Core's messages (`delivered`). Receipts only move forward.

Request:

```json
{ "id": "0123abcd-0123456789abcdef01234567", "state": "delivered" }
```

Response: `204`, no body.

Errors:

- `400` invalid receipt
- `404` message not found (or not sent to the caller)

Events: `peers.changed`.


<!-- file: http/projects.md -->

# Projects and skills

Projects are the connected Core's named work containers: a display name, zero or more directories on the machine running Core, a library directory Core keeps for that project, instructions, and a memory file. Skills are `SKILL.md` bundles discovered on that same machine. Installing or removing a bundle changes what a new conversation, or a conversation whose context is built again, can list. A conversation that already has a context keeps the catalog from when that context was built.

JSON responses use `Content-Type: application/json`. An error body is `{"error":"<message>","failure":{"code":"core_request_failed","message":"<message>","http_status":<status>,"details":"<message>"}}`.

A project object:

```json
{
  "id": "3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b",
  "name": "Demo",
  "primary": "/work/demo",
  "roots": ["/work/demo", "/work/notes"],
  "library": "/data/projects/3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b/library"
}
```

- `id` is assigned by Core. A new project receives a lowercase UUID. Creating a project again after it was removed can return the previous id; see `POST /v1/projects`.
- `name` is the display name, trimmed. Comparison for uniqueness ignores letter case.
- `primary` is the project's main directory, an absolute path on the machine running Core. It is always the first element of `roots`.
- `roots` is the directories the project keeps, primary first, then the others in the order they were saved. Duplicates of the same cleaned path appear once. The array is never null.
- `library` is the absolute path of the library directory Core derives for this id. It is present when Core has a data directory for projects. It is not one of `roots` unless the project has no folders. The request field is ignored.
- `folderless` is `true` when the project has no folders of its own. It is omitted when false. For that project, `primary` and `roots` are both the library path, and the library is created when the project is saved:

```json
{
  "id": "3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b",
  "name": "Notes",
  "primary": "/data/projects/3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b/library",
  "roots": ["/data/projects/3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b/library"],
  "folderless": true,
  "library": "/data/projects/3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b/library"
}
```

`GET /v1/projects` adds `status` on each project. `POST` and `PUT` return the project without `status`.

```json
{
  "available": true,
  "directories": [
    { "path": "/work/demo", "available": true },
    {
      "path": "/work/notes",
      "available": false,
      "reason": "invalid project cwd \"/work/notes\": no such file or directory"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `available` is true when the primary directory can be used. An additional directory that cannot be opened does not by itself make the project unavailable.
- `directories` lists each distinct root. `path` is that directory. `available` is false when it cannot be opened and listed. `reason` is then present and starts with `invalid project cwd "<path>"`.
- A library path that is not on disk yet counts as available. Core creates it on use. A library path that exists and is not a directory is unavailable.

A skill object:

```json
{
  "name": "brand",
  "description": "Apply the brand voice",
  "path": "/work/demo/.agents/skills/brand/SKILL.md",
  "source": "/work/demo",
  "digest": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

- `name` comes from the file's frontmatter: lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, at most 64 characters.
- `description` is the frontmatter description.
- `path` is the absolute path of that `SKILL.md` on the machine running Core.
- `source` is `global` for a skill installed for every conversation, the project directory the bundle was found under for a project skill, `builtin` for a skill shipped with Core, or `plugin:<name>` for a skill from an enabled plugin. The install response uses `global` or `project` instead; see `POST /v1/skills/install`.
- `digest` is 64 lowercase hex characters, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes.

`GET /v1/skills` returns `{"skills":[...],"warnings":[...]}`. Both arrays are present. `warnings` lists discovery problems; a bad bundle is skipped and the others are still returned. Project and global skills come first, ordered by name then path. Plugin skills follow, grouped by plugin name. Built-ins follow those. A project skill hides a global skill of the same name. A name already present hides a plugin skill and a built-in of that name. The same name under two project directories is two entries.

Built-in names are `web-search`, `widgets`, `hooks`, and `computer-use`. `computer-use` is left out when computer use is not available. A workspace or conversation list includes built-ins when Core has started browser support. The unscoped management list (`manage_scope=all` with no `session_id`, `project_id`, or `cwd`) includes built-ins whenever skills can be read from Core's home.

A skill whose frontmatter `requires` contains `library` is listed for a project that has a library, and in that unscoped management list. It is left out of every other list, including a conversation with no project.

### GET /v1/projects

Auth: any key
Effect: Lists the saved projects and whether their directories can be used right now, plus the operating system of the machine running Core.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "projects": [
    {
      "id": "3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b",
      "name": "Demo",
      "primary": "/work/demo",
      "roots": ["/work/demo", "/work/notes"],
      "library": "/data/projects/3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b/library",
      "status": {
        "available": true,
        "directories": [
          { "path": "/work/demo", "available": true },
          { "path": "/work/notes", "available": true }
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "host_os": "darwin"
}
```

- `projects` is the saved projects in the order they were saved, each with `status`. An empty Core returns `[]`.
- `host_os` is the operating system of the machine running Core, such as `darwin`, `linux`, or `windows`.

Errors:

- `500` the project list could not be read

Events: none.

### POST /v1/projects

Auth: any key
Effect: Saves a new project. Directories must already exist; this route does not create them. A project without folders gets a library directory instead, and that directory is created now. The response id may be a previous project's id: the latest removal of the same primary path after `.`, `..`, and extra separators are removed, or, for a project without folders, the latest removal of the same name including letter case. The directory match does not follow symlinks. If no removal was recorded for a project that has folders, a conversation still bound to that primary path can supply the old id. That id is reused once. Anything still stored for the id (conversations bound to it, instructions, library files, project memory) is there again with the recreated project.

Request:

```json
{ "name": "Demo", "primary": "/work/demo", "roots": ["/work/notes"] }
```

```json
{ "name": "Notes", "folderless": true }
```

- The body is one JSON object of at most 65536 bytes. Unknown fields are ignored. `id` and `library` are ignored.
- `name` (string) is required after trimming and at most 200 bytes. Names already saved are unique ignoring letter case.
- `folderless` (boolean) true creates a project with no folders. `primary` and every entry of `roots` must then be empty or absent. Core sets `primary` and `roots` to the new library path in the response.
- Without `folderless`, `primary` (string) is the main directory. `roots` (array of strings) lists additional directories. Each path is trimmed, then `.`, `..`, and extra separators are removed. It must be an absolute directory on the machine running Core and must be listable. The same path is kept once. At most 32 directories, including the primary.
- A project may be saved again later under a name it already has even when another project also has that name. Any other save that matches another project's name is refused.

Response: `200`

The saved project object. `folderless` is present only when true. `library` is present when Core has a data directory for projects.

Errors:

- `400` invalid project (the body is not JSON or is larger than 65536 bytes)
- `400` project name is required (maximum 200 characters)
- `400` a project without folders cannot also have directories
- `400` the project library is unavailable, so a project cannot be created without folders
- `400` use an absolute directory path on the Core host
- `400` invalid project cwd "<path>": the directory is missing, is not a directory, or cannot be listed
- `400` at most 32 project directories
- `400` the project could not be saved (the message says why)
- `409` another project already has this name

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/projects/{project}

Auth: any key
Effect: Replaces the registration of an existing project with the same checks as create. Directories already on disk are left where they are. Sending `folderless: true` drops the saved directories from the registration. Sending directories without `folderless` turns a project without folders into one that has those directories. The id does not change.

Path: `project` project id.

Request:

```json
{ "name": "Demo", "primary": "/work/demo", "roots": ["/work/notes"] }
```

- Same object and limits as `POST /v1/projects`. The id in the body is ignored; the path id is the project being saved.
- Omitted `folderless` means false. A project without folders is returned with `primary` and `roots` set to the library. Sending that object back is rejected. To save it again without folders, send `folderless: true`, `primary` `""`, and `roots` `[]`.

Response: `200`

The saved project object, as for `POST /v1/projects`.

Errors:

- `400` invalid project
- `400` the same directory and name failures as create
- `400` project not found
- `409` another project already has this name

Events: none.

### DELETE /v1/projects/{project}

Auth: any key
Effect: Forgets the registration. Directories, library files, instructions, project memory, and conversation bindings are left in place. A later create with the same primary path, or the same name for a project without folders, can take this id again.

Path: `project` project id.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "ok": true }
```

Errors:

- `404` project not found
- `500` the registration could not be updated

Events: none.

### POST /v1/projects/{project}/reveal

Auth: any key
Effect: Opens the project's primary directory in the file manager of the machine running Core. For a project without folders that directory is the library. Nothing is deleted.

Path: `project` project id.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "ok": true }
```

Errors:

- `404` project not found
- `500` the project list could not be read, the primary directory cannot be opened, or the file manager could not be started (`could not open the file manager on the Core host: ...`)

Events: none.

### GET /v1/projects/{project}/instructions

Auth: any key
Effect: Returns the project's instructions. A missing file is empty text. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Path: `project` project id.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "content": "",
  "version": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855",
  "max_chars": 16000
}
```

- `content` is the instruction text. Line endings are `\n`. Empty means there are no instructions.
- `version` is 64 lowercase hex characters, the SHA-256 of `content`. The empty text uses the SHA-256 of no bytes, including when the file is absent.
- `max_chars` is `16000`.
- A file edited outside this API is read up to 64000 bytes and then cut to the first 16000 characters. `version` matches that returned text.

Errors:

- `404` project not found
- `500` the project list or the instructions could not be read

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/projects/{project}/instructions

Auth: admin
Effect: Replaces the project's instructions when `expected_version` is still current. The text is what a conversation in this project receives the next time its context is built. A context already built keeps the previous text. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Path: `project` project id.

Request:

```json
{
  "content": "Always answer in French.",
  "expected_version": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
}
```

- The body is one JSON object of at most 256 KiB.
- `content` (string) is the new text. `\r\n` is stored as `\n`. Empty, absent, or only whitespace clears the instructions and removes the file. The text cannot contain a NUL and is at most 16000 characters after that newline change.
- `expected_version` (string) is required. It must be the `version` from the last read or the last successful save.

Response: `200`

The same object as `GET /v1/projects/{project}/instructions`, with the stored content and its new version.

Errors:

- `400` content and expected_version are required (JSON could not be read, the body is larger than 256 KiB, or `expected_version` is missing)
- `400` instructions cannot contain NUL
- `400` instructions are limited to 16000 characters
- `400` project instructions unavailable
- `400` the instructions could not be saved (the message says why)
- `404` project not found
- `409` instructions changed; refresh before saving
- `500` the project list could not be read

Events: none.

### POST /v1/projects/{project}/library

Auth: admin
Effect: Creates the project's library directory if it is not already there, and returns its path. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Path: `project` project id.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "path": "/data/projects/3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b/library" }
```

- `path` is the absolute library path. After `200` that path is a directory.

Errors:

- `404` project not found
- `500` project library unavailable, or the directory could not be created (the message says why)

Events: none.

### GET /v1/projects/{project}/memory

Auth: admin
Effect: Returns this project's memory text and the version a save must send back. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Path: `project` project id.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "content": "Uses pnpm.",
  "version": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "max_chars": 2200,
  "enabled": true
}
```

- `content` is the whole project memory file. A missing file is `""`. The text is not trimmed.
- `version` is 64 lowercase hex characters. It covers this project's text together with the global memory texts, so a change to either makes a later save stale.
- `max_chars` is `2200`.
- `enabled` is whether memory is turned on. The file is still returned when it is false.

Errors:

- `400` invalid memory project ID
- `404` project not found
- `500` the project list or the memory could not be read
- `503` memory is unavailable

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/projects/{project}/memory

Auth: admin
Effect: Replaces this project's memory file when `version` is still current, then returns the same view as the read. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Path: `project` project id.

Request:

```json
{
  "content": "Uses pnpm.\n\n---\n\nReports live in reports/weekly.",
  "version": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

- The body is one JSON object of at most 65536 bytes.
- `content` (string) is the whole file. Empty is allowed. At most 2200 characters. The text is stored as sent.
- Pieces of the previous text split on a line that is `---` with a blank line on each side, and no longer present in `content`, stay deleted: a later background review does not add that exact text back.
- `version` (string) is required and must be non-empty. Use the `version` from the last read or the last successful save of this project.

Response: `200`

The same object as `GET /v1/projects/{project}/memory`.

Errors:

- `400` content and version are required (JSON could not be read, the body is larger than 65536 bytes, or `version` is missing or empty)
- `400` invalid memory project ID
- `404` project not found
- `409` memory changed; refresh before saving
- `409` maximum 2200 characters
- `409` the memory could not be saved (the message says why)
- `500` the project list could not be read, or the memory was saved and the following read failed
- `503` memory is unavailable

Events: none.

### GET /v1/skills

Auth: any key
Effect: Lists skills for a conversation, a project, a directory, or the whole Core. A conversation that already has a context for its current workspace (same workspace kind, working directory, directories, and project) receives that captured catalog. Otherwise the response is a live reading and does not create a context. Reading skills for a project creates its library directory when it is missing.

Query: `session_id`, `project_id`, `cwd`, `manage_scope`, `q`. When more than one of `session_id`, `project_id`, and `cwd` is set, the first of those three in that order is the one that is used.

- `session_id` (string) is a conversation id. The list is that conversation's catalog, as above. A conversation with no workspace lists global skills (plus plugin and built-in skills under the rules above). A scratch conversation does not list project skills. The conversation's own directory is not scanned.
- `project_id` (string) is a project id. The list is a live reading for that project's directories. The library directory is scanned only when the project has no folders; otherwise skills are read from the project's own directories, skipping an additional directory that is missing.
- `cwd` (string) is an absolute directory on the machine running Core, used as one project directory with no library. Global skills are included. Skills that require a library are not.
- With none of those three, the list is the global skills, plus plugin and built-in skills, and skills that require a library are left out. `manage_scope=all` together with none of those three is the management list: a fresh reading of every available project's primary directory, plus global, plugin, and built-in skills, including skills that require a library. A project whose primary directory is unavailable is skipped.
- `manage_scope` (string) filters the list when it is set. `all` keeps every source. `global` keeps `source` `global`. `builtin` keeps `source` `builtin`. `project` keeps a source that is not `global`, not `builtin`, and does not start with `plugin:`. Any other value leaves `skills` empty. `warnings` is unchanged.
- `q` (string) is a case-insensitive substring of `name` or `description`. It applies only when `manage_scope` is set. An empty `q` does not narrow the list.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "skills": [
    {
      "name": "brand",
      "description": "Apply the brand voice",
      "path": "/work/demo/.agents/skills/brand/SKILL.md",
      "source": "/work/demo",
      "digest": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
    }
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

Errors:

- `400` invalid project cwd "<path>": workspace unavailable; restore the directory or choose another location
- `404` session not found
- `404` project not found
- `500` the workspace or the project list could not be read, or the library directory could not be created

Events: none.

### POST /v1/skills/install

Auth: admin
Effect: Fetches one `SKILL.md` from an `http` or `https` URL and writes it onto the machine running Core. `scope` `global` installs it for every conversation. `scope` `project` installs it under that project's primary directory (the library, when the project has no folders). Scripts in the bundle are not run. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request:

```json
{
  "url": "https://192.0.2.10/skills/brand/SKILL.md",
  "scope": "project",
  "project_id": "3f2a1c0e-6b7d-4e18-9c0a-1b2d3e4f5a6b",
  "expected_digest": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

- The body is one JSON object of at most 8192 bytes and may contain only these fields.
- `url` (string) is required, at most 2048 characters, `http` or `https`, with a host and no user name. A local or private address is rejected, including after DNS lookup and on a redirect. The fetch gives up after 20 seconds. The file must be at most 256 KiB and must be a skill file: frontmatter between `---` lines, a `name` and a `description` as in the skill object above, and `requires` containing only `library` when it is present. Other frontmatter fields are ignored.
- `scope` (string) is `global` or `project`.
- `project_id` (string) is required when `scope` is `project`, and must be an existing project whose primary directory is available.
- `expected_digest` (string) is optional. When it is sent, it must equal the digest of the fetched file or nothing is written.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "skill": {
    "name": "brand",
    "description": "Apply the brand voice",
    "path": "/work/demo/.agents/skills/brand/SKILL.md",
    "source": "project",
    "digest": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
  },
  "context_reload_required": true
}
```

- `skill` is the installed file. `path` is where it was written. `source` is the request `scope`, `global` or `project`, which is not the `source` a later `GET /v1/skills` returns for a project skill.
- `context_reload_required` is always `true`. A conversation that already has a catalog does not list the new skill until its context is built again.

Errors:

- `400` invalid Skill install request (the body is not a JSON object of these fields, or is larger than 8192 bytes)
- `400` scope must be global or project
- `400` project_id is required for project Skills
- `400` the URL or the file was rejected. Stable messages include `URL is required and must be at most 2048 characters`, `URL must be an http or https address`, `local and private network URLs are not allowed`, `could not fetch Skill: ...`, `Skill URL returned HTTP <status>`, `could not read Skill: ...`, `SKILL.md exceeds 256 KiB`, `missing YAML frontmatter`, `unterminated YAML frontmatter`, `invalid name or description`, and `unknown requires "<value>" (only library)`
- `400` project directories are unavailable
- `404` project not found
- `409` Skill changed after preview; preview it again
- `409` Skill is already installed; remove it before reinstalling
- `500` the project list could not be read, the destination could not be checked, or the file could not be written

Events: none.

### POST /v1/skills/uninstall

Auth: admin
Effect: Removes one global or project skill that was listed for an available project primary directory or for every conversation. The `SKILL.md` file is deleted. The directory that contained it is removed only when that leaves the directory empty; any other file there is kept. Built-in skills, plugin skills, and a skill that exists only under an additional project directory are left in place. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request:

```json
{
  "path": "/work/demo/.agents/skills/brand/SKILL.md",
  "expected_digest": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

- The body is one JSON object of at most 8192 bytes and may contain only these fields.
- `path` (string) is required. It must be absolute and already cleaned: the same string Core returned in `path`, or another absolute path that resolves to that file, with no `.` or `..` and no trailing separator.
- `expected_digest` (string) must equal that skill's current `digest`.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "skill": {
    "name": "brand",
    "description": "Apply the brand voice",
    "path": "/work/demo/.agents/skills/brand/SKILL.md",
    "source": "/work/demo",
    "digest": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
  },
  "context_reload_required": true
}
```

- `skill` is the catalog entry that was removed. `source` is `global` or the project directory, as in `GET /v1/skills`.
- `context_reload_required` is always `true`. A conversation that already has a catalog keeps listing the skill until its context is built again.

Errors:

- `400` path and expected_digest are required (the body is not a JSON object of these fields, is larger than 8192 bytes, or `path` is empty)
- `404` Skill is not removable
- `409` Skill changed; refresh the list and try again (this is also the result when `expected_digest` is empty)
- `500` the file could not be removed

Events: none.


<!-- file: http/runs.md -->

# Runs: sending, streaming, stopping

These routes start a turn, watch it, stop it, and change what is waiting to be sent. A turn belongs to Core: closing the HTTP response does not stop it. `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns` is the stream for the client that sent the turn. Anyone else, and that client after a dropped connection, attaches with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events`. Stop only with `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel`. Revoking the access key that started a live turn stops it. Replacing that key does not.

`{id}` is a conversation handle. A session id is its main lane: a UTC timestamp `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS`, then `_`, then a UUID, for example `2026-10-14T12-04-05_018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3b`. Another lane is that id, `~`, and a lane name (`draft` gives `…a3b~draft`). A lane name is 1 to 48 characters, starts with a letter or digit, then letters, digits, `_` or `-`, and is never `main`. Lanes of one session run at the same time. Each has its own turn, queue, goal, questions and run stream. Codex, Grok, pi and Claude run only on the main lane.

JSON responses are `application/json`. A usual error is

```json
{"error":"session not found","failure":{"code":"core_request_failed","message":"session not found","http_status":404,"details":"session not found"}}
```

`error` is the message to show. The three routes that answer `409` with a different body say so below. Timestamps are UTC.

Core-wide notifications (`GET /v1/events`) and run-stream frames (`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events` and the body of `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns`) are specified in [Events](../events.md). This file says how to open, resume and close those streams.

## Run state

`state` on `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/run-state`, and the `state` of a pause or resume:

- `idle` — nothing is running, and no task is waiting to be continued.
- `running` — a turn is in progress.
- `pausing` — pause was requested; work already started is finishing. New work waits.
- `paused` — paused. Continue with `resume` or stop with `cancel`.
- `waiting_children` — running, and the turn is waiting for child tasks.
- `interrupted` — the task stopped and can be continued. A turn that finished with messages still queued is `interrupted`, with `reason` `追加消息已保存，请继续处理`.
- `blocked` — the task cannot continue until the owner acts. `reason` says why.

`reason` is that explanation, or `""`.

## Goal

`status` is `active`, `paused`, `blocked`, `complete`, `usage_limited` or `capped`.

An `active` goal keeps starting another turn after a turn that finishes normally, up to the goal continuation cap (`goal_max_continuations` of `GET /v1/task-limits`, 100 by default; `continuations` counts those). The owner stopping a turn leaves the goal as it is. A turn that fails becomes `blocked`, or `usage_limited` when the failure is a provider usage limit. Reaching the cap becomes `capped` with `reason` `<cap> automatic continuations`. `resume`, and an edit that starts the goal again, set `continuations` back to 0. They do not spend one.

`pause` does not stop a turn that is already running. That turn finishes, and no further goal turn starts until `resume`. `clear` removes the goal and also leaves a running turn alone.

The first turn of a newly set goal shows `objective` as the owner's message. Later goal turns are hidden continuation turns.

A goal turn may wait (the model's `wait_goal`): the turn ends with no continuation after it, and the lane's [wake](#wakes) starts the next goal turn later, counted as one continuation. Any `POST …/goal` action cancels the wait.

## Wakes

A wake is one deferred turn of a lane: when it is due, Core starts a turn whose first message is hidden (`internalMessage` `wake`). A lane has at most one pending wake; setting another replaces it. Wakes survive a Core restart. A wake waits while its lane runs and fires when the lane is free. `source` is `goal` (a goal waiting), `plugin:<name>` (a plugin, such as the loop plugin's next check) or `api`. Deleting or archiving the conversation drops its wakes.

A wake object:

```json
{
  "id": "wk_0c1d2e3f405162738495a6b7",
  "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3b",
  "source": "plugin:loop",
  "due_at": "2026-10-14T12:34:05Z",
  "note": "build 41 running",
  "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:04:05Z"
}
```

`note` is absent when empty. Times are UTC.

## Message input

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns` and `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` take the same input fields.

- `prompt` (string). Required unless `attachments` is non-empty. Codex, Grok, pi and Claude also reject a prompt that is only whitespace.
- `attachments` (array of strings, optional). Ids of images already stored for this conversation. Each id is 64 lowercase hex characters. At most 20 images, at most 40 MiB together. A model that does not accept images is rejected.
- `references` (array, optional). At most 64. Each object has `type`, `label` (at most 200 Unicode characters; may be `""`), and the fields for its type:
  - `file` or `directory`: `path`, an absolute path on the Core host inside this workspace. A file is a regular file. A directory is a directory.
  - `host_path`: `path`, an absolute path of a file or directory anywhere on the Core host. Optional `kind` is `file` or `directory` and must match. Core sets `outside_workspace`.
  - `skill`: `path`, the absolute path of a skill available in this workspace. Core replaces `label` with the skill's name.
  - `session`: `session_id` of a conversation that exists.
- `input_placements` (array, optional). At most 84. Each object is `marker` (string, 1 to 256 characters, appearing exactly once in `prompt`), `type` (`reference` or `image`) and `index` (which reference or attachment). The marker is not sent as text. It is where that reference or image sits. Anything not listed is appended after the prompt.

## Pending list

`GET`, `PATCH` and `POST …/pending-messages/…` return:

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "id": "queued_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "prompt": "Also check the tests",
      "mode": "steer",
      "editable": true
    }
  ],
  "executor": "native",
  "actions": {"edit": true, "front": true, "insert": true, "send_now": true},
  "insert_note": ""
}
```

- `messages` is an array, empty when nothing is waiting. Order is delivery order.
- `id` is the id sent with the message, or `queued_` plus 32 hex characters when the client omitted one.
- `prompt` is the message text.
- `mode` is `steer` or `queue`. `steer` can enter at the next step. `queue` waits until the current work takes a follow-up. A Grok turn always stores follow-ups as `queue`.
- `editable` is true only when the message is a single text block. Attachments or references make it false.
- `image_count` (number) is present only when the message has images.
- `delivering` (true) is present only while this message is being handed to the live turn. It cannot be deleted or reordered then.
- `held` (true) and `held_until` (UTC, to the second) are present only while an edit hold is active. See `hold`.
- `executor` is `native` (Gyres), `codex`, `grok`, `pi` or `claude`.
- `actions.edit` and `actions.front` are true. `actions.insert` and `actions.send_now` are true only while a turn is live (not while it is still preparing). For Grok, `insert` is true only when that turn can take text immediately.
- `insert_note` is `""`, or `grok_timing_not_guaranteed` for Grok: Grok decides when inserted text is used.

A hold lasts 2 minutes and is kept only in memory. Another `hold` refreshes it. Delivery does not pass a held message at the front of the queue. `release`, a successful edit, or expiry clears it. A restart drops every hold.

### GET /v1/events

Auth: any key
Effect: Opens the Core-wide notification stream. The first frame is `ready`. The stream then forwards notifications until the client disconnects or Core closes it (Core is reloading). There is no resume cursor: connect again. The server does not read a last-event id. If this client falls behind, a later frame is `resync`; refetch anything you were watching. Frames and fields are in [Events](../events.md).

Request: no body.

Response: `200` `text/event-stream`

`Cache-Control: no-cache` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` are set. Each notification is one `data:` line of JSON and a blank line. There is no `id:` line. About every 20 seconds the stream sends a comment line `: heartbeat`. Ignore lines that start with `:`.

Errors:

- `503` Core is reloading. Connect again.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events

Auth: any key
Effect: Attaches to the turn already running in this conversation, without starting one. A dropped connection continues from the last frame it handled. Closing this response does not stop the turn.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Query: `stream` and `after`, or `history_cursor`. All optional.

- `stream` is the `X-Gyres-Run-Stream` value from the stream you were reading (16 lowercase hex characters). `after` is the SSE `id` of the last frame you handled, a decimal byte offset. Both are required together. They are accepted only for this turn's own stream and only when `after` is the end of a frame. The server does not read a last-event id header.
- `history_cursor` is the `history_cursor` returned with this conversation's transcript. It resumes an external-agent turn (Codex, Grok, pi, Claude) after that transcript. A Gyres turn does not resume this way.
- `stream` and `after` are tried first. If they do not match, `history_cursor` is tried. Anything else replays the turn from the beginning: a missing or unknown cursor, a cursor from an earlier turn, a turn with no resume marks, or a position that is not on this stream.

Request: no body.

Response: `200` `text/event-stream` while a turn is running.

`Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. `X-Gyres-Run-Stream` names this turn's stream. `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Gyres-Run-Stream`.

Each frame is a `data:` line of JSON, then an `id:` line (the offset to pass back as `after`), then a blank line. About every 10 seconds the stream sends `: heartbeat`, which has no `id`. If the progress stream breaks, one frame is sent and the response ends:

```json
{"type":"stream_error","error":"progress stream unavailable; reload conversation"}
```

That frame has no `id`. Reload the transcript.

When `stream`/`after` or `history_cursor` resumes, the first frame is `{"type":"run_resume","session_id":"<id>"}` with no `id`. Keep the transcript you already show, then apply only the frames after it. A full replay starts at the beginning of the turn; replace what you show with that baseline before applying later frames. Frame fields are in [Events](../events.md).

The response stays open until the turn finishes or you disconnect. After it ends, read the transcript for the result.

Response: `204` no body, when nothing is running (including a task that is paused, blocked or interrupted but not live).

`X-Gyres-History-Version` is an opaque version of the stored history. `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Gyres-History-Version`. Compare it with `history_version` from the transcript you just loaded. The same value means nothing ran in between.

Response: `409` while the turn is preparing and cannot be observed yet. Retry.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `409` turn is preparing; retry observation

Events: none.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/run-state

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports whether this conversation is idle, running, paused, or waiting to be continued. Read this after a dropped stream, or when `session.task` says the task changed.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{"state":"running","reason":""}
```

`state` and `reason` are [Run state](#run-state). `reason` is always present.

Errors:

- `404` session not found

Events: none.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/pending-messages

Auth: any key
Effect: Lists messages waiting to enter the running turn, or still waiting on a task that can be continued. While a turn is preparing, the list is what is already queued and `insert` and `send_now` are false.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200` the [pending list](#pending-list).

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `500` the waiting list could not be read

Events: none.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/goal

Auth: any key
Effect: Returns this conversation's goal, or `null` when it has none. Does not start or change a turn.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "goal": {
    "id": "018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3b",
    "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3b",
    "objective": "Ship the parser fix",
    "status": "active",
    "provider_id": "openai",
    "model": "gpt-4.1",
    "continuations": 0,
    "created": "2026-10-14T12:04:05Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-14T12:04:05Z"
  }
}
```

```json
{"goal": null, "wake": null}
```

`wake` is the goal's pending wait (a [wake](#wakes) with source `goal`), or `null`.

- `id` is a UUID. `session_id` is the conversation handle.
- `objective` is the text the owner set.
- `status` and `continuations` are [Goal](#goal).
- `provider_id` and `model` are present when the goal was given a model. Its turns use that model.
- `reason` and `stopped_at` are present when the goal stopped continuing (`blocked`, `usage_limited`, `capped`). Both are cleared when it is `active` again.
- `blocker` and `blocker_turns` are present while a blocker is being counted. `blocker_this_turn` is true when the turn still running has reported one.
- `created` and `updated` are UTC.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `503` goals are unavailable
- `500` the goal could not be read

Events: none.

### GET /v1/wakes

Auth: any key
Effect: Lists every pending wake, soonest first. Changes nothing.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{"wakes": [{"id": "wk_0c1d2e3f405162738495a6b7", "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3b", "source": "plugin:loop", "due_at": "2026-10-14T12:34:05Z", "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:04:05Z"}]}
```

Each entry is a [wake](#wakes).

Events: `session.wake` on `GET /v1/events` whenever a lane's wake is set, replaced, cancelled, fired or dropped.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/wake

Auth: any key
Effect: Returns the lane's pending wake, or `null`. Changes nothing.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{"wake": null, "running": false}
```

- `wake` is a [wake](#wakes) or `null`.
- `running` is true while a turn of the lane runs.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `503` wakes are unavailable

Events: none.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/subagents

Auth: any key
Effect: Lists child tasks this conversation dispatched, and names the parent when this conversation itself is a child. Children are separate conversations. Their turns, queues and streams are their own.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "children": [
    {
      "session_id": "child_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "task_id": "task_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "name": "parser",
      "call_id": "call_1",
      "delivered": false,
      "cwd": "/work/parser",
      "state": "running",
      "reason": ""
    }
  ],
  "parent_session": ""
}
```

- `children` is an array, empty when there are none. A child id is `child_` plus 32 hex characters. `task_id` is `task_` plus 32 hex characters.
- `name` is the short name given when it was dispatched. `call_id` is the dispatch id, or `""` when the child was found only from its own task.
- `delivered` is true after the parent has been given the outcome.
- `outcome` is present once delivered, and is the recorded result state (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or another task state).
- `cwd` is present only when the child's working directory differs from the parent's.
- `state` while the child runs is `running`, `pausing` or `paused`, otherwise the task state (`interrupted`, `blocked`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`). A child whose start was never recorded is `failed` with `reason` `子任务启动记录不完整`. After delivery, `state` is `outcome`, or `completed` when no outcome was stored, and `reason` may be `已交付；后续执行见子会话`.
- `reason` is present when the task has one.
- `result` is present once the child has finished and is not still running. It is the child's assistant text, cut at 16000 characters with a trailing `\n[Result truncated; use session_search with child session ID for full history.]`, plus the task error when there is one. After delivery it is the summary stored at delivery.
- `parent_session` is the parent's conversation id, or `""` when this conversation is not a child.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `500` a child's result could not be read

Events: none.

### GET /v1/sessions/{id}/user-questions

Auth: any key
Effect: Lists questions a live turn is waiting on. A new question is also announced as `session.question` on `GET /v1/events`. The list is empty when nothing is waiting. Order is not significant. Questions live only in memory; a restart drops them.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3c",
      "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-04-05_018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3b",
      "tool_call_id": "call_1",
      "questions": [
        {
          "id": "library",
          "header": "Library",
          "question": "Which HTTP client?",
          "options": [
            {"label": "net/http", "description": "Use the standard library"},
            {"label": "req", "description": "Use a third-party client"}
          ]
        }
      ],
      "created": "2026-10-14T12:04:05Z",
      "deadline": "2026-10-14T12:05:05Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `id` is the batch id (a UUID). Pass it as `{qid}` when answering.
- `session_id` is the conversation. `tool_call_id` is the tool call that asked.
- `questions` holds 1 to 3 questions. Each `id` is unique in the batch. `header` and `question` are short text. `options` holds 2 or 3 objects with `label` and `description`. The first option is the one a timeout selects.
- `created` and `deadline` are UTC. The deadline is 60 seconds after `created`. After it, the turn continues with the first option of each question and this batch disappears.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `503` ask_user_question is unavailable

Events: none.

### POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns

Auth: any key (administrator key when this turn uses Codex, Grok, pi or Claude and that agent does not allow non-administrators)
Effect: Starts one turn and returns its run stream. The turn is accepted before the stream is attached. Closing the response does not stop it. Reattach with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events`. The request is not idempotent: after an ambiguous failure, read the conversation before sending again. Sending `provider_id` and `model` stores them as this conversation's model when that choice differs from the saved one.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request:

```json
{
  "prompt": "Fix the parser and add a test",
  "provider_id": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-4.1",
  "cwd": "/work/app",
  "attachments": ["0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"],
  "references": [{"type": "file", "path": "/work/app/parser.go", "label": "parser"}],
  "input_placements": [{"marker": "@parser", "type": "reference", "index": 0}]
}
```

- Message fields are [Message input](#message-input). `prompt` may be `""` when `attachments` is non-empty.
- `provider_id` and `model` (strings, optional). Omit both to use this conversation's model, then the settings default, then the first available model. If either is sent, that pair is used as given. A conversation whose saved model is no longer available fails until another model is chosen.
- `reasoning_effort` and `service_tier` (strings, optional) apply only when the model is Codex, Grok, pi or Claude. Empty means the model's default. `service_tier` is rejected for Grok, pi and Claude, and must be one Codex offers (`default` is accepted). A provider model rejects either field.
- `cwd` (string, optional) is the working directory for this turn. Empty uses the conversation's workspace.
- `system_prompt` (string, optional) replaces the default style for a provider model. A blank value keeps the default. A Bot conversation ignores it. Codex, Grok, pi and Claude reject a non-empty value.
- `context_settings` (object, optional) is rejected for Codex, Grok, pi and Claude. For a provider model, `context_window` is an integer from 4096 to 10000000. `output_reserve`, `keep_recent_tokens`, `summary_max_tokens` and `threshold_tokens` are optional integers; omitted or 0 uses 4096, 20000, 2048, and `context_window - output_reserve`. The summary must fit in the output reserve, recent messages must fit under the threshold, and the threshold must leave the output reserve inside the window.
- `max_turns` (integer, optional) caps steps of this task. When a global cap is enabled, a missing or higher value is lowered to that cap. A lower value is kept.

Response: `200` `text/event-stream`

Same headers, heartbeats and frames as `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events`. This response always starts at the beginning of the turn. Keep `X-Gyres-Run-Stream` and the last `id` if you need to reconnect. The stream stays open until the turn finishes.

Errors:

- `400` invalid json
- `400` missing prompt
- `400` the prompt, references, attachments or placements were rejected. Stable messages include `unknown reference type`, `at most 64 references`, `reference label too long`, `too many input placements`, `invalid or duplicated input marker`, `invalid reference placement`, `invalid image placement`, `invalid input placement type`, `A message can contain at most 20 images`, `Images in one message exceed the 40 MiB limit`, `Invalid attachment ID`, `Image attachment not found`, `The selected model does not support images; remove the images or choose another model`
- `400` unknown or unconfigured model, or `missing endpoint or model`
- `400` `This conversation's model setting (<model>) is no longer available. Choose another model.`
- `400` `Model options currently require an external agent`
- `400` `context_window must be between 4096 and 10000000`, or `invalid context budgets: reserve output and leave room for summary plus recent messages`
- `400` invalid project cwd, when `cwd` cannot be used
- `400` `Bot conversations run on a configured provider, not an external agent`
- `400` `<Label> cannot run in a branch of a conversation` (Codex, Grok, pi or Claude on a lane)
- `400` `<Label> is disabled in Settings → External agents`
- `400` the agent is not installed or not signed in. Codex: `Codex is unavailable; check External agents settings and run codex login on the Core host`. Grok: `Grok is unavailable; check External agents settings and run grok login on the Core host`. pi: `pi is unavailable; check External agents settings and configure a model in pi on the Core host`. Claude: `Claude is unavailable; check External agents settings and sign in to Claude Code in a terminal on the Core host`
- `400` `unknown Codex model`, `Unsupported Codex reasoning effort`, `Unsupported Codex service tier`, and the same kind of message for Grok (`unknown Grok model`, `Unsupported Grok reasoning effort`, `Grok does not support service tiers`), pi (`unknown pi model`, `Unsupported pi thinking level`, `pi does not support service tiers`) and Claude (`unknown Claude model`, `Unsupported Claude effort level`, `Claude does not support service tiers`)
- `400` `<Label> manages its own instructions and context` when `system_prompt` or `context_settings` is sent to Codex, Grok, pi or Claude
- `403` `Ask an administrator to turn on "Allow non-administrators" for <Label> in Settings → External agents.`
- `404` session not found
- `409` `This conversation uses <Label>; start a new conversation to switch agents`
- `409` `<Label> conversation workspace cannot change`
- `409` `Start a new conversation to use Codex` (or Grok, pi, Claude) when that agent is asked to take a conversation that already has history
- `409` `子会话请通过父任务追加工作` — this conversation is a child; send further work from the parent
- `409` `任务尚未完成，请先继续或停止` — a task is still open
- `409` `turn already running`, or for an external agent `turn already running or awaiting recovery`
- `409` the task is waiting and nothing is live. The body is not the usual error envelope:

```json
{"error":"Gyres is waiting to be continued; continue or stop it first","code":"awaiting_continuation","agent":"Gyres","state":"interrupted"}
```

`agent` is `Gyres`, `Codex`, `Grok`, `pi` or `Claude`. `state` is the [run state](#run-state).

- `409` stop won before the turn was accepted. Nothing was recorded. The body is not the usual error envelope:

```json
{"error":"stopped before the turn started","code":"turn_stopped"}
```

- `500` the turn could not be saved or the progress stream could not be created (`cannot create progress stream`, `cannot read task limits: …`)
- `503` `storage unavailable; reconnect and retry`, or `Core is moving its data directory; try again when it finishes`

Events: `session.run_started`, `session.run_finished`, `session.messages`, `session.task`. Naming a model that changes the conversation's setting also emits `session.settings`.

### POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel

Auth: any key
Effect: Stops the live turn, or marks a task that is waiting (paused, interrupted, blocked, or still running with no live turn) as cancelled. Child tasks of this turn are stopped too. When the turn belongs to a scheduled task, that occurrence is cancelled. The response can arrive before the stream has closed. A second stop, when nothing is left, conflicts.

Path: `id` conversation handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{"session_id":"2026-10-14T12-04-05_018f3a2b-7c4d-7e5f-a6b7-8c9d0e1f2a3b","canceled":true}
```

`canceled` is always true on success. Follow `run-state` or the run stream until the live turn has left; then `state` is `idle`.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `409` no active turn
- `500` `task stopped, but cancellation could not be saved: …` — the turn was still stopped

Events: `session.task`, `session.run_finished`. A child that was stopped emits `session.task` for the child and for this conversation.

### POST /v1/sessions/{id}/{action}

Auth: any key (administrator key to resume a Codex, Grok, pi or Claude conversation when that agent does not allow non-administrators)
Effect: Pauses or resumes this conversation's turn. `pause` stops new work and lets work already started finish (`pausing`, then `paused`). It does not cancel the turn. `resume` continues a paused live turn, or starts a task that is waiting and has no live turn. Children follow the parent's pause. Codex, Grok, pi and Claude have no pause; stop them with `POST …/cancel`.

Path: `id` conversation handle. `action` is `pause` or `resume`. Any other value is `404`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{"state":"paused"}
```

`state` is the [run state](#run-state) after the change: `pausing` or `paused` for pause, `running` when resume opens a live turn. Resuming a task that the log has already finished does not start a turn; `state` is then whatever `GET …/run-state` would report.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `404` unknown action
