Path: `id` session id or lane handle.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "recap": {
    "text": "The layout is sketched.",
    "next": "Add the empty state.",
    "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:20:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json
{ "recap": null }
```

`text` is the recap. `next` is the suggested next message and may be `""`. `created_at` is when it was stored. `transcript_size` is not included.

Errors:

- `404` session not found
- `500` the recap could not be read

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/recap

Auth: admin
Effect: Stores this lane's recap. An ordinary key is refused before the conversation is looked up. `text` and `next` are trimmed, then clipped to 400 and 200 Unicode code points; a clipped value ends with `…`. `if_transcript_size` must equal the transcript route's current `transcript_size`, including `0` for an empty transcript. The recap can be stored while the recap plugin is off; `GET` then still returns `null` until the plugin is on. `created_at` is set when the recap is stored.

Path: `id` session id or lane handle.

Request:

```json
{
  "text": "The layout is sketched.",
  "next": "Add the empty state.",
  "if_transcript_size": 4096
}
```

- `text` (string) is required and must not be blank after trimming.
- `next` (string, optional) is the suggested next message.
- `if_transcript_size` (integer) is required.
- The body is one object of at most 65536 bytes and may contain only these fields. An unknown field is rejected with the same status as a missing `text`.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "ok": true }
```

Errors:

- `403` administrator key required
- `400` text and if_transcript_size are required
- `404` session not found
- `409` transcript changed
- `500` the recap could not be saved

Events: `session.recap`


<!-- file: http/storage.md -->

# Storage, export and import

These routes tell a frontend where this Core keeps its data, move that data to another directory, delete a previous location, reopen Core when the directory is missing or broken, delete old archived conversations, and download or restore one zip of the whole Core. Every route needs the administrator key.

JSON responses are `application/json` and send `Cache-Control: no-store`.

While Core is opening its data directory, or reopening after a move, import, retry or reset, every request is `503` with `code` `core_starting`, `error` `Core is starting; try again in a moment`, and `Retry-After: 5`. The reopen starts about 300 ms after the response that asked for it. Poll `GET /v1/storage` until `started_at` changes; that value is the UTC time this process opened.

While a move or an import is in progress, `GET /v1/storage` still returns `200`. Every other route in this file returns `503` with `code` `storage_maintenance`, `error` `Core is moving its data directory; try again when it finishes`, and `Retry-After: 5`.

While the data directory is unavailable, routes under `/v1/storage` still answer. Export, import and archive cleanup return `503` with `code` `storage_unavailable`. A Core that could not open its data directory at startup serves the storage routes only; the other routes here get that same `503`, and `error` names the reason, the path and the message.

A hard failure latches unavailable at once and emits `storage.unavailable`. Those reasons are `invalid`, `missing`, `not_directory`, `not_writable`, `read_only`, `full` and `identity_mismatch`. A transient failure (`timeout`, or `io_error` from the check itself) does not latch on the first miss. Other routes can wait up to 10 seconds for the check, then return `503` with `code` `storage_slow` and an `error` beginning `storage is slow to respond; waiting`. `GET /v1/storage` then has `mode` `slow`. The wait becomes a latch after 20 seconds without a success, counted from the first failing check, and `unavailable.reason` is then `timeout` or `io_error`. Routes under `/v1/storage` are not held by that wait.

Those `503` bodies, and any other error built the same way, look like this. `failure.message` and `failure.details` repeat `error`.

```json
{
  "error": "Core is moving its data directory; try again when it finishes",
  "code": "storage_maintenance",
  "failure": {
    "code": "core_request_failed",
    "message": "Core is moving its data directory; try again when it finishes",
    "http_status": 503,
    "details": "Core is moving its data directory; try again when it finishes"
  }
}
```

An error with no top-level `code` has `error` and `failure` only. `failure.http_status` is the HTTP status. Where a route describes its own body, that body is the whole response.

`storage.space` is `{"type":"storage.space","level":"low","volume":"data"}`. `level` is `ok`, `low` or `critical`. `volume` is `data` or `home`. `storage.unavailable` is `{"type":"storage.unavailable","reason":"missing"}`. `sessions.changed` carries `session_id`.

Seven directories move with the data location, in this order: `sessions`, `workspaces`, `schedules`, `tasks`, `bot`, `code`, `projects`. Everything else stays in the home directory.

Free space has two levels. `low` means free space is below the larger of 2 GiB and 5% of the volume. `critical` means free space is below 512 MiB. Leaving `low` takes 256 MiB above its line; leaving `critical` takes 128 MiB above 512 MiB. A `low` or `critical` level does not change `mode` and does not by itself reject a request.

`running` entries, where a route returns them, use `kind` and `id`. `title` is omitted when empty. The array is not ordered.

- `run`: a conversation run. `id` is the conversation id, shaped `2026-10-14T12-00-00_` plus a UUID.
- `memory_review`: a background memory review. `id` is `memory`.
- `complete`: a model request still in flight. `id` is `complete`.
- `task`: a running task receipt. `title` is the agent name when it has one.
- `subagent`: a running receipt that belongs to a parent conversation. `title` is the agent name when it has one.
- `schedule`: a schedule occurrence that has not finished. `title` is the schedule name.

### GET /v1/storage

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports where data is stored, how full the disks are, and whether a move, an import or a storage failure is in progress. In normal mode this read also checks free space on the data volume and the home volume.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

Normal mode. `categories` is always the seven directories, in the order above. Sizes are omitted outside normal mode.

```json
{
  "mode": "normal",
  "slow": null,
  "home": "/srv/gyres",
  "data_dir": "/srv/gyres-data",
  "default": false,
  "restart_required": false,
  "started_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00.123456789Z",
  "categories": [
    {"name": "sessions", "bytes": 1048576, "files": 12},
    {"name": "workspaces", "bytes": 0, "files": 0},
    {"name": "schedules", "bytes": 0, "files": 0},
    {"name": "tasks", "bytes": 0, "files": 0},
    {"name": "bot", "bytes": 0, "files": 0},
    {"name": "code", "bytes": 0, "files": 0},
    {"name": "projects", "bytes": 4096, "files": 1}
  ],
  "total_bytes": 1052672,
  "total_files": 13,
  "free_bytes": 20000000000,
  "space": {
    "data": {"free_bytes": 20000000000, "total_bytes": 500000000000, "level": "ok"},
    "home": {"free_bytes": 8000000000, "total_bytes": 250000000000, "level": "low"},
    "same_volume": false,
    "checked_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:01Z"
  },
  "migration": {
    "state": "idle",
    "bytes_done": 0,
    "bytes_total": 0,
    "files_done": 0,
    "files_total": 0
  },
  "unavailable": null,
  "cleanup": {"path": "/srv/gyres-old", "bytes": 4096}
}
```

A move in progress. Category sizes, `total_bytes`, `total_files` and `free_bytes` are absent. Poll about once a second.

```json
{
  "mode": "maintenance",
  "slow": null,
  "home": "/srv/gyres",
  "data_dir": "/srv/gyres",
  "default": true,
  "restart_required": false,
  "started_at": "2026-10-14T11:00:00.100000000Z",
  "migration": {
    "state": "running",
    "phase": "copying",
    "target": "/srv/gyres-data",
    "bytes_done": 4096,
    "bytes_total": 1052672,
    "files_done": 1,
    "files_total": 13
  },
  "unavailable": null,
  "cleanup": null
}
```

The data directory cannot be used. `default_data` is present only in this mode when `data_dir` is not the home path.

```json
{
  "mode": "unavailable",
  "slow": null,
  "home": "/srv/gyres",
  "data_dir": "/srv/gyres-data",
  "default": false,
  "restart_required": false,
  "started_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00.123456789Z",
  "migration": {
    "state": "idle",
    "bytes_done": 0,
    "bytes_total": 0,
    "files_done": 0,
    "files_total": 0
  },
  "unavailable": {
    "reason": "missing",
    "path": "/srv/gyres-data",
    "message": "the directory does not exist (is the disk connected?)"
  },
  "default_data": {
    "path": "/srv/gyres",
    "has_data": true,
    "bytes": 1048576,
    "moved_at": "2026-10-13T18:00:00Z"
  },
  "cleanup": {"path": "/srv/gyres"}
}
```

- `mode` is `unavailable` when `unavailable` is set, otherwise `maintenance` while a move or import holds the Core, otherwise `slow` while a transient failure is being waited out, otherwise `normal`.
- `slow` is null when nothing is being waited out. Otherwise `reason` is `timeout` or `io_error`, `path` is the data directory, `message` is the check error, and `since` is the UTC time of the first failing check.
- `home` and `data_dir` are absolute paths. `default` is true when those two strings are equal.
- `started_at` is UTC. Fractional seconds appear when the clock has them. It changes on every reopen.
- `restart_required` is true when `migration.state` is `restart_required`. Maintenance stays on until the new process answers.
- `categories[].name`, `bytes` and `files` are logical file sizes. `total_bytes` and `total_files` sum them. `free_bytes` is free space on the data volume; it is omitted when that read fails.
- `space` is omitted until a check has succeeded. A failed check on this read keeps the previous `space` and still returns `200`. `checked_at` is UTC, whole seconds. `same_volume` is true when both paths are on one volume; `home` and `data` then carry the same numbers. On one shared volume a level change emits `storage.space` for `data` and for `home`.
- `migration.state` is `idle`, `running`, `failed` or `restart_required`. `phase` is omitted while idle. A data move uses `copying`, `verifying`, `rewriting`, `switching`, then `done`. An import sets `kind` to `import` and uses `unpacking`, `verifying`, `placing`, `rewriting`, `switching`, then `done`. `target` is the destination path, omitted for an import. `error` is set when `state` is `failed`. Byte and file counters stay `0` until the copy or unpack has measured work.
- `unavailable.reason` is one of the latch reasons above. `free_bytes` and `needed_bytes` appear when a retry still finds a full disk: `needed_bytes` is 536870912 (512 MiB). `message` is then `The disk still has only <free> free. Free up space until at least <needed> is free, then try again.` Sizes in that sentence use `GiB`, `MiB`, or a byte count.
- `unavailable.reason` can also be `stopping` after a retry that is waiting for runs to finish. `message` is `tasks are still stopping (N); try again shortly`.
- `default_data.path` is the home path. `has_data` is true when the home still has files in the seven directories, even when `bytes` is `0`. `moved_at` is present when the recorded previous location is the home path. It is UTC, whole seconds.
- `cleanup` is null when no previous location is waiting. Otherwise `path` is that location. `bytes` is included only in normal mode and is the size of the seven directories there. A directory that is a link is not added to `bytes`.

Errors:

- `500` the seven directories could not be measured. Normal mode only. The body is `error` and `failure`.

Events: `storage.space`

A level change found by this read emits `storage.space`. The first observation of `ok`, and a read that does not change a level, emit nothing.

### POST /v1/storage/check

Auth: admin
Effect: Checks whether the data can be moved to `path`. Nothing is copied and the target directory is not created. `ok` false is still `200`; read `items`.

Request:

```json
{ "path": "/srv/gyres-data" }
```

- `path` is required. Surrounding whitespace is removed. Any other field is ignored. The body is at most 4096 bytes.
- `allow_non_empty` is accepted and ignored here. `POST /v1/storage/migrate` is what acts on it.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "path": "/srv/gyres-data",
  "default": false,
  "items": [
    {"id": "absolute", "ok": true, "message": "The path is absolute."},
    {"id": "usable", "ok": true, "message": "The directory exists and is empty."},
    {"id": "writable", "ok": true, "message": "The location is writable."},
    {"id": "separate", "ok": true, "message": "The location is separate from the current data directory."},
    {"id": "space", "ok": true, "message": "21474836480 bytes free, 537952256 needed."},
    {"id": "idle", "ok": true, "message": "Nothing is running."}
  ],
  "running": [],
  "total_bytes": 1052672,
  "allocated_bytes": 1081344,
  "reserve_bytes": 536870912,
  "required_bytes": 537952256,
  "free_bytes": 21474836480
}
```

- `ok` is true only when every item has `ok` true. A warning item still has `ok` true.
- `path` is the cleaned absolute path. A relative path is returned unchanged.
- `default` is true when `path` is the home directory, including when a link resolves to it. That is a move back to the default location. On success the saved data directory is cleared; it is not set to the home path.
- `items` stay in this order: `absolute`, `usable`, `writable`, `separate`, `space`, then `size` when measuring the current data failed, then `cleanup` when a previous location is still recorded, then `idle`.
- A relative path fails `absolute` with `The path must be absolute.` The next four items fail with `Not checked: the path must be absolute first.`
- `usable` passes when the directory exists and is empty, or when it can be created under an existing parent (`The directory will be created.`). A path that exists and is not a directory fails. A directory that cannot be read fails. Names `.DS_Store`, `.localized`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini` and names starting with `._` are ignored.
- A directory that already holds any other entry passes `usable` with `warning` true and sets `existing`. `existing.count` is the full count. `existing.names` is at most the first five, in filename order. `message` is `The directory is not empty (N items); Gyres will copy its folders next to them and leave them untouched.`
- `usable` fails when any entry name matches a moved directory or `.gyres-storage-id`, ignoring case. `message` is `The directory already holds <name> from a Gyres data directory; choose another folder.`
- For a move back, `usable` passes with `The default location holds no earlier data.` when each of the seven directories is missing or empty. Empty directories and the ignored names do not count. A file or a link in place of one of them counts. Otherwise `usable` fails and `leftover` is set.
- `leftover.categories` lists each home directory that still has files, with `name`, `bytes` and `files`. `leftover.bytes` and `leftover.files` are the sums. `recorded` is true when that leftover is the previous location of a move away from the home, and `moved_at` is the UTC time of that move when known. `message` then says to delete the old data first. When `recorded` is false, `message` names the folders and says they must be moved or deleted by hand.
- `writable` probes the directory, or the existing parent when the target does not exist yet. A permission error is quoted. On macOS a permission error also appends a note about the first-access prompt for a removable volume.
- `separate` fails when the target is the current data directory, is inside it, contains it, or overlaps a moved directory that is itself a link. For a move back it fails with `Gyres already uses the default location.` or when current data overlaps one of the seven directories in the home. A data directory that lives inside the home is allowed.
- `space` compares `free_bytes` with `required_bytes`. `free_bytes` is `0` when the path is not absolute or the free-space read fails. `allocated_bytes` rounds each current file up to 4 KiB (an empty file counts as 4 KiB). `reserve_bytes` is 536870912. `required_bytes` is the larger of the stored size plus 10% and the stored size plus `reserve_bytes`. When short, `short_bytes` is the gap and `message` is `Needs <required> bytes (the data as stored plus 10%, keeping at least <reserve> bytes free) but only <free> bytes are free: short by <short> bytes.` A passed check says `<free> bytes free, <required> needed.`
- `size` fails with `Cannot measure current data: ` plus the reason. `cleanup` fails with `Clean up the previous location (<path>) before moving the data again.` `idle` fails with `<N> task(s) are still running; wait for them or stop them first.` `running` lists that work.

Errors:

- `400` `path required`. Invalid JSON, a body over 4096 bytes, or a missing or blank `path`. The body is `error` and `failure`.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/storage/migrate

Auth: admin
Effect: Runs the same check as `POST /v1/storage/check`, then copies the seven directories to `path` and reopens Core on that location. The previous location is kept and recorded for `POST /v1/storage/cleanup`.

Request:

```json
{ "path": "/srv/gyres-data", "allow_non_empty": false }
```

- `path` is required, with the same rules as the check.
- `allow_non_empty` is optional and defaults to false. It is required when the check sets `existing`. It does not override a failed item. A move back that still has `leftover` stays failed; this flag does not delete that leftover.

Response: `202`

```json
{
  "state": "running",
  "phase": "copying",
  "target": "/srv/gyres-data",
  "bytes_done": 0,
  "bytes_total": 0,
  "files_done": 0,
  "files_total": 0
}
```

- This is the `migration` object. Totals fill in on a later `GET /v1/storage`, after the copy has measured the directories. `kind` is omitted.
- For a move back, `target` is the home path.
- Phases are `copying`, `verifying`, `rewriting`, `switching`. Success sets `state` to `restart_required` and `phase` to `done`, then Core reopens. Failure sets `state` to `failed` and `error` to the reason, leaves `phase` where it stopped, and ends maintenance.
- Poll `GET /v1/storage` until `started_at` changes. A failed move leaves the previous data in place.

Errors:

- `400` `path required`, same as the check.
- `503` `storage_unavailable`, `the current data directory is unavailable; retry it or switch back to the default first`. `Retry-After: 5` and the coded failure body.
- `409` `storage_maintenance`, `a migration is already running`, when this call loses the race to start maintenance. `Retry-After: 5` and the coded failure body. Once maintenance is on, a later call is the shared `503` instead.
- `422` the check did not pass, or it passed with `existing` and `allow_non_empty` is false. Maintenance is turned off again. The body has no `code` and no `failure`. `error` is `the target failed the pre-check`, or `the target is not empty; confirm with allow_non_empty` when `check.ok` is true and `existing` is set. `check` is the full `200` body of `POST /v1/storage/check`.

Events: `storage.unavailable`

Emitted only if the data directory fails during the copy.

### POST /v1/storage/cleanup

Auth: admin
Effect: Deletes the seven directories at the recorded previous location, then clears that record. The directory now in use is not deleted. A moved directory that is a link is removed as a link; the directory it points at is kept.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "path": "/srv/gyres-old",
  "removed": ["sessions", "workspaces", "projects"]
}
```

- `path` is the location that was recorded.
- `removed` lists the seven names that were present, in the order given above. Names that were already absent are left out. An empty result is `[]`.

Errors:

- `409` `storage_maintenance`, `the data directory is not ready`, when the data directory is unavailable or maintenance is on. `Retry-After: 5` and the coded failure body. While a move is already in progress the shared `503` usually answers first.
- `404` `no old location to clean up`. `error` and `failure` only.
- `409` `the current data directory is not healthy: ` plus the reason. The current location must still be the registered data directory.
- `409` `the old location is not the original data directory`.
- `409` `the old location overlaps the current data directory: ` plus the directory path. Nothing further is deleted after this refusal. Directories earlier in the list may already have been removed when a later delete returns `500`.
- `500` the delete or the record update failed. `error` is `delete <path>: <reason>` or the underlying error. The record remains until a later call succeeds. Call the route again.

Events: `storage.unavailable`

Emitted only if the health check latches the data directory.

### POST /v1/storage/retry

Auth: admin
Effect: Re-checks an unavailable data directory and reopens Core when it is usable again. When storage is already available this returns the same `200` document as `GET /v1/storage` and does not reopen.

Request: no body.

Response: `202`

```json
{ "recovered": true }
```

Core reopens. Until `started_at` changes, requests are `503` `core_starting`.

A retry that does not reopen returns `200` and the `GET /v1/storage` document, with `mode` still `unavailable`. The `unavailable` object is the result of this attempt.

- `reason` `stopping` and `message` `tasks are still stopping (N); try again shortly` while a run slot is still held. Call again when it is clear. A full disk is remembered: the next attempt still requires 512 MiB free.
- `reason` `full` when the disk is still below 512 MiB. `free_bytes` and `needed_bytes` are set, and `message` is the free-space sentence from `GET /v1/storage`. If free space cannot be read, `message` is `Cannot read the free space: ` plus the reason, without those two numbers.
- Any other check failure uses that failure's `reason` and `message`. `path` is the configured data directory.
- Success requires an existing writable directory. When Core has a saved identity for that directory, the identity file there must match. A directory Core has never opened successfully is accepted by this route once it is an existing writable directory. A directory with a different identity is refused with `identity_mismatch`.

Core also runs this check every 5 seconds while latched, and reopens by itself when the directory is back with its saved identity and, for a full disk, 512 MiB free. That timer does not adopt a directory that has never been opened successfully. A different identity is not adopted.

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/storage/reset

Auth: admin
Effect: Clears a custom data location and reopens Core on the home directory. Files at the custom location are left where they are. This is only for the unavailable state.

Request: no body.

Response: `202`

```json
{ "reset": true, "data_dir": "/srv/gyres" }
```

- `data_dir` in this body is the home path the new process will use. The saved custom location is cleared, so the next `GET /v1/storage` reports `default` true and `data_dir` equal to `home`.
- A cleanup record that names the home path is removed, because that path is now the live data. A record that names some other path is kept.
- Whatever the home directory already holds is what comes back. The two locations are not merged.

Errors:

- `409` `the data directory is available; use migration to move it`.
- `409` `already using the default data directory`.
- `409` `tasks are still stopping; try again shortly`, while a run slot is still held.
- `500` the setting could not be saved.

Each of these is `error` and `failure` only.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/archive-cleanup

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports the automatic deletion of archived conversations and the last run, if one has been recorded.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "days": 90,
  "last_run": {
    "at": "2026-10-14T03:00:00Z",
    "trigger": "auto",
    "days": 90,
    "deleted": 2,
    "skipped": 1,
    "freed_bytes": 1048576
  }
}
```

- `enabled` is false when the setting has never been saved. `days` is `30`, `90` or `180`. A missing setting, a missing file, or a stored value outside those three is reported as `90`.
- `last_run` is omitted when no run has been recorded, the record cannot be read, or `at` is empty.
- `at` is UTC, whole seconds. `trigger` is `auto` or `manual`. `days` is the value used for that run. `deleted`, `skipped` and `freed_bytes` are numbers. `error` is omitted when the run listed the archive successfully.
- While `enabled` is true, Core checks five minutes after it opens and then every hour. It runs when the last run, manual or automatic, is at least 24 hours before `at`. It does not start during a move or while storage is unavailable.

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### PUT /v1/archive-cleanup

Auth: admin
Effect: Saves the automatic cleanup switch and the age threshold. The response is the same document as `GET /v1/archive-cleanup`.

Request:

```json
{ "enabled": true, "days": 30 }
```

- `days` is required and must be `30`, `90` or `180`.
- `enabled` defaults to false when omitted, which turns the switch off.
- Unknown fields are rejected. The body is at most 128 KiB.

Response: `200`

The `GET /v1/archive-cleanup` document, after the save.

Errors:

- `400` `invalid settings request`. Invalid JSON, unknown fields, or a body over 128 KiB.
- `400` `days must be 30, 90 or 180`.
- `500` the setting could not be saved.

Each of these is `error` and `failure` only.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/archive-cleanup/run

Auth: admin
Effect: Deletes archived conversations older than the saved `days`, including when the switch is off. The response is the `GET /v1/archive-cleanup` document, with this run as `last_run` and `trigger` `manual`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

The `GET /v1/archive-cleanup` document.

- Age uses the transcript's modification time. A conversation is deleted when that time is before now minus `days` times 24 hours.
- Bot chats are left in place and are not counted.
- A conversation that is running or pinned counts in `skipped` and is kept.
- A conversation that is restored, or whose transcript time changes after the run listed it, is kept and counts in neither `deleted` nor `skipped`.
- `freed_bytes` sums, before each delete, that conversation's files in the sessions directory, its presented files, its widgets and its agent binding files. The scratch work directory is not counted and is not removed.
- One run at a time. A second call waits for the first and then returns `200`.
- If a move starts or storage becomes unavailable during the run, the run stops after the conversation it is on and records the counts so far. `error` stays empty in that case.
- A failure to list the archive is still `200`. `last_run.error` is the reason, and the counts stay `0`.

Errors: none.

Events: `sessions.changed`

One event per conversation removed, with that conversation's `session_id`. A run that removes nothing emits none.

The download and the upload share one lock. A second export or import gets `409` `transfer_busy`.

The package is a zip. `manifest.json` is the last entry. Its `format` is `gyres-export` and `format_version` is `1`. A client that only saves or uploads the body can treat the zip as opaque. The fields below are what import checks and what `GET /v1/import` repeats from the last package.

```json
{
  "format": "gyres-export",
  "format_version": 1,
  "gyres_version": "1.2.3",
  "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
  "source": {
    "os": "linux",
    "home": "/srv/gyres",
    "data": "/srv/gyres-data",
    "parts": {"sessions": "/srv/gyres-data/sessions"}
  },
  "categories": [
    {"id": "conversations", "files": 12, "bytes": 1048576},
    {"id": "settings", "files": 1, "bytes": 512}
  ],
  "secrets_to_reenter": [
    {"kind": "provider", "name": "Northwind"},
    {"kind": "plugin", "name": "example", "keys": ["token"]},
    {"kind": "mcp", "name": "Example tools"},
    {"kind": "channel", "name": "feishu"}
  ],
  "excluded": [
    "access keys",
    "TLS certificates and keys",
    "provider API keys",
    "plugin secrets",
    "MCP credentials and OAuth tokens",
    "Bot channel connections",
    "logs",
    "caches (browser, runtimes)",
    "updates",
    "storage records",
    "external agents' own histories"
  ],
  "entries": [
    {"path": "conversations/sessions/2026-10-14T12-00-00_018f3a2c-7b14-4c3e-9a10-6d2e4f8a1b00.jsonl", "size": 128, "sha256": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "mode": 384}
  ]
}
```

- `source.parts` maps every part id (`sessions`, `workspaces`, `visualizations`, `projects`, `memories`, `bot`, `skills`, `schedules`, `tasks`, `code`, `plugins`, `approvals`) to its directory. The example shows one. `source.resolved`, when present, maps a part id to that same directory with symlinks resolved, and only for parts where the two paths differ.
- `categories[].id` is `conversations`, `projects`, `memory`, `bot`, `skills`, `schedules`, `tasks`, `code`, `plugins`, `approvals`, then `settings`. `files` and `bytes` count packed files. Empty parts are still listed. `excluded` is always the list in the example.
- `mode` on a file entry is the permission bits as a number. `384` is owner read and write.
- `secrets_to_reenter[].kind` is `provider`, `plugin`, `mcp` or `channel`. `keys` is present for a plugin and lists the secret names that had a value, not the values. `provider` uses the provider name, or its id when the name is empty. `channel` uses the kind, `feishu` or `discord`.
- API keys, the data location, the listen address, LAN discovery, TLS and trusted proxies are removed from the packed settings. Access keys, certificates, plugin secrets, MCP credentials, Bot channel connections, logs and caches are not packed. `excluded` names those groups.
- A file entry omits `type` and includes `size` and a 64-character `sha256`. `mode` is the permission bits. `mtime` is omitted when zero. A directory has `type` `dir`. A link has `type` `link` and `target`, and is not a zip entry of its own.
- Paths are relative and use `/`. They sit under `conversations/sessions`, `conversations/workspaces`, `conversations/visualizations`, `projects/projects`, `memory/memories`, `bot/bot`, `skills/skills`, `schedules/schedules`, `tasks/tasks`, `code/code`, `plugins/plugins`, `approvals/approvals`, or `settings/` with one of `config.json`, `mcp-servers.json`, `codex.json`, `grok.json`, `pi.json`, `claude.json`, `hooks.json`, `running-input.json`. `bot/bot/channels` and `plugins/plugins/.tmp` are not valid entries.

### GET /v1/export

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports the current or last export. The counters stay after the export finishes; `idle` means no export has run in this process.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "state": "running",
  "files_done": 4,
  "files_total": 13,
  "bytes_done": 4096,
  "bytes_total": 1052672,
  "at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
}
```

- `state` is `idle`, `running`, `done` or `failed`.
- `files_total` and `bytes_total` are measured from the part directories when the export starts. They include files the zip then leaves out, so `files_done` can finish below `files_total` when `state` is `done`. Settings files are in the zip and are not part of these counters.
- `at` is UTC and is omitted while `idle`. It is the start time while `running`, and the finish time when `done` or `failed`.
- `error` is present only when `state` is `failed`.

```json
{
  "state": "idle",
  "files_done": 0,
  "files_total": 0,
  "bytes_done": 0,
  "bytes_total": 0
}
```

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/export

Auth: admin
Effect: Streams a zip of this Core's data. Export does not enter maintenance. Nothing may be running, and no other export or import may be in progress.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

`Content-Type: application/zip`. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="gyres-export-20261014-120000.zip"`. The timestamp is the Core host's local time, `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`. `Cache-Control: no-store`. The body is the package described above.

The status is `200` as soon as the body starts. A read error after that aborts the connection. `GET /v1/export` then has `state` `failed` and `error` set. Poll that route for `files_done` while the download runs.

Errors:

- `409` work is still running. The body has no `failure` object:

```json
{
  "error": "1 task(s) are still running; wait for them or stop them first",
  "code": "transfer_busy",
  "running": [{"kind": "run", "id": "2026-10-14T12-00-00_018f3a2c-7b14-4c3e-9a10-6d2e4f8a1b00"}]
}
```

- `409` `an export or import is already running`, with `code` `transfer_busy` and no `running` field.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/import

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports whether an import is in progress, whether this Core is fresh enough to accept one, and the outcome of the last import.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "running": false,
  "not_fresh": [],
  "last": {
    "state": "done",
    "at": "2026-10-14T12:05:00Z",
    "gyres_version": "1.2.3",
    "created_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
    "categories": [
      {"id": "conversations", "files": 12, "bytes": 1048576}
    ],
    "secrets_to_reenter": [
      {"kind": "provider", "name": "Northwind"}
    ]
  }
}
```

- `running` is true only while an import holds the transfer lock, including during the upload before `POST /v1/import` answers. An export in progress leaves it false. After the import is accepted, maintenance hides this route until the import fails or Core reopens. Follow progress on `GET /v1/storage`.
- `not_fresh` is always an array. An empty array means a package can be imported. Otherwise the ids are the categories that already hold data, in this order, skipping empty ones: `conversations`, `projects`, `memory`, `bot`, `skills`, `schedules`, `code`, `plugins`.
- `conversations`: a non-empty transcript (`*.jsonl`) under sessions, or any other user file under workspaces or visualizations.
- `projects`: `projects.json` is not a JSON array, or that array is not empty, or projects has any other user file.
- `memory`: a Markdown file that is not empty or whitespace.
- `bot`: a non-blank `MEMORY.md`, or any file under `incidents/`.
- `skills`, `schedules` and `code`: any user file. `plugins`: any user file outside `.tmp`.
- Ignored names are the same as on the storage check, plus `.lock`. A link, any other non-directory, and a directory that cannot be read count as data. What a new Core writes for an empty Bot chat, default settings and blank memory files does not.
- `last` is omitted when no import has been recorded or the record cannot be read.
- `last.state` is `done` or `failed`. `at` is when this Core finished the attempt. `created_at` and `gyres_version` come from the package. `created_at` is omitted when the package had none. `error` is omitted unless `state` is `failed`.
- `categories` and `secrets_to_reenter` are copied from the package. `skipped_links` lists package paths of links that were not created because the target would fall outside this Core's home or data directory. It is omitted when there are none.

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/import

Auth: admin
Effect: Reads a package from the request body, checks it, and replaces this Core's data with the package. The Core must be fresh and idle. On success Core reopens. Poll `GET /v1/storage` for `migration.kind` `import`. After the reopen, `GET /v1/import` carries `last`.

Request: the zip bytes. The content type is not checked. This is not JSON and not a multipart form.

- The upload must fit in the free space of the data volume above a 512 MiB reserve. An empty body is refused.

Response: `202`

```json
{
  "kind": "import",
  "state": "running",
  "phase": "unpacking",
  "bytes_done": 0,
  "bytes_total": 1048576,
  "files_done": 0,
  "files_total": 12
}
```

- `files_total` and `bytes_total` count file entries in the manifest. Directories and links are not included. `target` is omitted.
- Phases are `unpacking`, `verifying`, `placing`, `rewriting`, `switching`. Success sets `state` to `restart_required` and `phase` to `done`, then Core reopens. Failure sets `state` to `failed` and `error`, ends maintenance, and records `last.state` `failed` with the same error.
- The package replaces every part it knows. A part the package does not carry becomes empty.
- This machine keeps its data location, listen address, LAN discovery, TLS, trusted proxies, and any API key already stored here. Providers that exist only here are kept. MCP connections come back without credentials.
- Paths that pointed at the source Core are rewritten onto this Core. A link whose target would fall outside the home or the data directory is skipped and named in `last.skipped_links`.
- If the data directory sits inside a `.gyres-import` directory under the home, the import fails after the `202` with `the data directory <path> is inside the import staging folder; move it first`.

Errors:

The `409` and `422` bodies below have `error` and `code`, plus the extra fields named. They have no `failure` object. A refusal before the `202` leaves this Core unchanged.

- `503` `storage_unavailable`, `the data directory is not ready`, when this call finds storage unavailable or maintenance already on. `Retry-After: 5` and the coded failure body.
- `409` `transfer_busy`, `an export or import is already running`.
- `409` `transfer_busy`, with `running`, when work is in progress. `error` is `<N> task(s) are still running; wait for them or stop them first`.
- `409` `import_not_fresh`, with `categories` set to the `not_fresh` ids. `error` is `Import needs a fresh Gyres: this one already holds <names>. Merging into existing data is not supported yet.`
- `409` `transfer_busy`, `a data move is running`, when maintenance cannot be entered. If the second idle and fresh check fails after maintenance starts, maintenance ends and the `409` above is returned instead.
- `422` `import_upload`. `error` is `Cannot receive the package: ` plus the reason. An empty body uses `the request body is empty`. Too little free space uses `the data disk has only <size> free` or `not enough free space on the data disk (<size> free)`.
- `422` `import_invalid`. `error` is one of:
  - `this file is not a Gyres export package (not a readable zip)`
  - `this file is not a Gyres export package (no manifest.json)`
  - `this file is not a Gyres export package` when `format` is not `gyres-export`
  - `cannot read manifest.json: <reason>` or `manifest.json is damaged: <reason>`
  - `this package was made by a newer Gyres (format N); update Gyres, then import it`
  - `this package has an unknown format version (N)` when the version is below 1
  - `the package lists <name> twice`
  - `the package has an invalid or repeated entry: "<path>"`
  - `the package is incomplete: <path> is missing`
  - `the package is damaged: <path> does not match the manifest` when size or `sha256` does not match
  - `the package has an invalid entry: "<path>"`
  - `the package has an unknown entry type "<type>"`
  - `the package holds <name>, which the manifest does not list`
- `422` `import_space`. `error` is `Cannot read free space: <reason>`, or `Not enough free space at <directory>: the import needs <need> and keeps <reserve> free, but only <free> is free.` The data volume and the home volume are checked separately. On one volume the two needs are added. Each side must keep 512 MiB free. Need is the packed files rounded up to 4 KiB.

Events: `storage.unavailable`

Emitted only if the data directory fails during the import.


<!-- file: http/system.md -->

# System

Status, identity, disk and process counters, model-usage records, the task-round cap, HTTPS, desktop and standalone updates, and the managed browser and code runtimes. These routes do not change a conversation.

JSON responses are `application/json`. A failed request uses the usual error body (`error` plus `failure`) except where an endpoint shows another body. Do not match on `error` text; branch on the HTTP status and, where an endpoint gives one, on `code`.

While Core is opening, `GET /health` answers `503` at once. Every other route in this file waits up to 10 seconds for Core to finish opening, then answers the same `503`: `code` is `core_starting`, `Retry-After` is `5`. That starting answer does not require an access key. While the data directory is unavailable or being moved, `GET /health`, `GET /v1/identity`, `POST /v1/identity/challenge`, `GET /v1/version`, `GET /v1/tls` and `POST /v1/tls/issue` keep their normal answers. Every other route here then answers the storage `503` (`storage_unavailable`, `storage_maintenance` or `storage_slow`).

Timestamps are UTC, RFC3339, and may include a fraction of a second.

### GET /health

Auth: none
Effect: Reports that this Core process is accepting requests. A `200` means the process is up. It does not mean the data directory is usable, and it does not mean HTTPS is on.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "status": "ok" }
```

- `status` is the string `ok`.
- `X-Gyres-Core-Instance` is always set. It is an opaque token for this process, or an empty string when Core was not given one. A frontend can ignore it.
- `X-Gyres-Core-Mode` is set only when this Core has a build channel. The value is `production`, `develop` or `local`.
- The `503` returned while Core is still opening does not send these two headers and does not use this body.

Errors:

- `503` Core is still opening (`code` `core_starting`, `Retry-After: 5`). Retry. This route does not wait.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/browser-runtime

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports the managed browser on this Core host: whether it is installed, and how far a running install has got. Nothing is downloaded by this call.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "phase": "downloading",
  "percent": 30,
  "progress": "12/40 MB (30%)",
  "state": "installing",
  "supported": true,
  "binary": "/var/lib/gyres/browser/bin/agent-browser",
  "chrome": "/var/lib/gyres/browser/chrome/chrome",
  "version": "0.38.1",
  "log": "/var/lib/gyres/browser/install.log"
}
```

- `state` is `missing` (not installed), `installing`, `ready` or `error`. When the browser program and Chrome are both present and no install is running, the state is `ready` and `error` is cleared.
- `phase` is omitted when there is nothing to report. During an install it is one of `checking`, `binary`, `downloading`, `extracting`, `verifying` and `ready`. It is not saved across a restart: after a restart a ready browser omits `phase`.
- `percent` is 0–100 while a download reports a percentage, and is omitted when the size is unknown or a download is being retried.
- `progress` is a short progress string, such as `12/40 MB (30%)`, or `正在重新下载` while a download is retried. Omitted when empty.
- `error` is omitted when empty. On failure it is the install error. The text can name a path on the Core host.
- `supported` is true on macOS Apple silicon, Linux amd64, Linux arm64, Windows amd64 and Windows arm64.
- `binary` is the path of the browser program on the Core host. It is present even when the file is not there yet.
- `chrome` is the path of the Chrome executable. Omitted when none is published.
- `version` is the browser release this Core installs (`0.38.1`).
- `log` is the path of the install log on the Core host. It is present before the first install.
- The response is not `Cache-Control: no-store`. Poll this route while `state` is `installing`. An install gives up after 15 minutes and then `state` is `error`.

Errors:

- `503` the managed browser is not running in this Core. The body is only `{"error":"Browser unavailable"}`, with no `failure`.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/code-runtime

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports the managed code runtime (a pinned runtime used to run code) on this Core host. Nothing is downloaded by this call.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "state": "installing",
  "version": "1.4.2",
  "binary": "/var/lib/gyres/runtimes/bun/1.4.2/bun",
  "downloaded": 1048576,
  "total": 20971520
}
```

- `state` is `missing`, `installing`, `ready` or `error`. Core starts an install when it opens, on a host that supports it.
- `version` is the runtime release this Core installs (`1.4.2`).
- `binary` is the path of that runtime on the Core host.
- `error` is omitted when empty. After a failed install it holds the reason.
- `downloaded` is how many bytes of the archive have been written. `total` is the archive size in bytes, or `-1` when the download did not say a length. Both stay at `0` until a download starts, and are not cleared when `state` becomes `ready`. Use `state`, not these two numbers, to decide readiness.
- Only macOS on Apple silicon can install this runtime. Other hosts come up with `state` `error`.

Errors:

- `503` the code runtime is not running in this Core. The body is only `{"error":"code runtime unavailable"}`, with no `failure`.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/identity

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports which kind of access key this request used, and where this Core can be reached. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "role": "admin",
  "host": "studio",
  "instance_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "addresses": [
    { "url": "https://core.example.com", "source": "https" },
    { "url": "http://192.0.2.10:15100", "source": "lan" },
    { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:15100", "source": "loopback" }
  ]
}
```

- `role` is `admin` when the key is an administrator key, and `user` for every other accepted key.
- `host` is the operating-system hostname of the Core machine. It is an empty string when that name cannot be read.
- `instance_id` is 32 lowercase hex characters, stable for this Core's home across restarts. Clients that know several addresses use it to recognise one machine. It is an empty string when it cannot be stored.
- `addresses` is never null. Each `url` is an origin a client can use, and `source` says why it is listed. Order, with duplicates removed:
  1. `https` — the HTTPS address, only while HTTPS state is `active` or `renewal_failing`. The port is omitted when it is 443.
  2. `listen` — `http://` plus the HTTP bind address and port, only when HTTP is bound to one non-loopback IPv4 address.
  3. `lan` — one `http://<ipv4>:<port>` for each up, non-loopback IPv4 address, only when HTTP listens on every interface. Private addresses come first.
  4. `loopback` — `http://127.0.0.1:<http port>`, always.
- Only IPv4 is listed, apart from the HTTPS URL, which uses the configured domain. If the machine's addresses cannot be listed, the `lan` entries are skipped and `loopback` remains.

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/resources

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports this process and how much disk Core's files use. The disk figures are measured at most once every 30 seconds; the process figures are read on every call.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "sampled_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
  "host": "studio",
  "os": "linux",
  "arch": "amd64",
  "home": "/var/lib/gyres",
  "data_dir": "/var/lib/gyres",
  "pid": 1234,
  "logical_cpus": 4,
  "go_version": "go1.25.0",
  "heap_bytes": 1000000,
  "go_reserved_bytes": 8000000,
  "goroutines": 40,
  "active_runs": 1,
  "uptime_seconds": 3600,
  "storage": {
    "measured_at": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
    "bytes": 10,
    "files": 1,
    "partial": false,
    "skipped": 0,
    "categories": [
      {
        "id": "conversations",
        "bytes": 10,
        "files": 1,
        "home_bytes": 10,
        "data_bytes": 0,
        "home_files": 1,
        "data_files": 0,
        "moves": true
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `sampled_at` is when this response was built. `host` is the operating-system hostname, or empty when it cannot be read.
- `os` and `arch` name the Core host, such as `linux` and `amd64`, or `darwin` and `arm64`.
- `home` and `data_dir` are absolute paths on the Core host. They are equal when data has not been moved. `pid` is this process. `logical_cpus` is the number of logical CPUs. `go_version` is the Go runtime version. `heap_bytes` is the heap in use. `go_reserved_bytes` is memory reserved from the operating system. `goroutines` is the number of goroutines. `active_runs` is how many conversation runs are in this process now. `uptime_seconds` is whole seconds since this process started.
- `storage.measured_at` is when the disk scan ran. A call within 30 seconds of that time returns the same `storage` object, including a `partial` one. Wait until `measured_at` is 30 seconds old before expecting a new scan.
- `bytes` and `files` are logical sizes of regular files, counted once. Symlinks are not followed and are not counted. `partial` is true when the scan stopped early (2 seconds, 100,000 entries, or an entry that could not be read). `skipped` counts entries that were not measured: unreadable entries, symlinks and files that are not regular.
- `categories` contains only ids that have at least one counted file, largest `bytes` first, then `id` ascending. `home_bytes` / `home_files` are the part under `home`. `data_bytes` / `data_files` are the part under `data_dir` when that path is different; otherwise they are `0` and the whole total is in the home fields. A data directory inside the home is not counted twice.
- `id` is one of `conversations`, `browser`, `code`, `bot`, `runtimes`, `workspaces`, `memory`, `skills`, `plugins`, `visualizations`, `mcp`, `approvals`, `access`, `logs`, `cache`, `backups`, `tasks`, `other`.
- `moves` is true for `conversations`, `workspaces`, `tasks`, `bot` and `code`: those follow the data location. Every other id stays with the home.

Errors:

- `500` Core home unavailable

Events: none.

### GET /v1/task-limits

Auth: any key
Effect: Reads the global cap on how many model rounds a new task may run. The cap is off until someone saves one. A task already running keeps the cap it started with.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "enabled": false, "max_turns": 100, "goal_max_continuations": 100 }
```

- `goal_max_continuations` caps a goal's automatic continuations ([goal](runs.md#goal)); `100` until someone saves another.
- `enabled` is false until a cap is turned on. While it is false, new tasks are not capped, and `max_turns` is still stored.
- `max_turns` is the stored cap. When no setting has been saved it is `100`. A new task is limited to this many model rounds only when `enabled` is true. One round is one model decision and its tool calls. A tighter limit asked for on a single task is kept; this setting never raises a task's own limit.

Errors:

- `500` the saved setting could not be read

Events: none.

### GET /v1/tls

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports HTTPS: whether it is on, the certificate that is being served, and any order waiting on the owner. Secrets are not included. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "state": "active",
  "https_url": "https://core.example.com",
  "host": "",
  "port": 443,
  "domain": "core.example.com",
  "source": "acme",
  "cert_file": "",
  "key_file": "",
  "acme": {
    "ca": "letsencrypt",
    "directory_url": "",
    "staging": false,
    "email": "owner@example.com",
    "challenge": "dns-01",
    "http01_port": 80,
    "dns_provider": "cloudflare"
  },
  "credentials": {
    "cloudflare.api_token": { "set": true },
    "eab.kid": { "set": false },
    "eab.hmac": { "set": false }
  },
  "certificate": {
    "issuer": "Example CA",
    "subject": "core.example.com",
    "names": ["core.example.com"],
    "not_before": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
    "not_after": "2026-12-30T00:00:00Z",
    "serial": "0a1b2c3d",
    "staging": false
  },
  "last_attempt_at": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
  "last_renewal_at": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
  "next_renewal_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z",
  "last_error": null,
  "listen_error": null,
  "pending": null,
  "propagation": "checked",
  "handshake_errors": 0
}
```

- `enabled` is whether HTTPS is turned on. `state` is decided in this order: `disabled` when it is off; `error` when the saved settings cannot be read or do not validate; then, for an ACME setup with no certificate yet, `waiting_owner` while a manual TXT record is waiting to be added, `issuing` while an order is running or has been asked for, `pending_issue` when no order has been asked for or the last problem was only a warning, otherwise `error`. With a certificate loaded: `listen_failed` when the HTTPS port is not open; `waiting_owner` again while a manual TXT record waits; `expired` when the certificate is outside its dates; `renewal_failing` for an ACME certificate whose latest problem is not a warning; otherwise `active`.
- `https_url` is `https://` plus `domain`, with `:<port>` only when `port` is not 443, while a certificate is loaded and the listener is up. Otherwise it is null. Identity lists this URL only in `active` and `renewal_failing`.
- `host` is the HTTPS bind address. An empty string means every interface. `port` is the HTTPS port; a saved `0` is reported as `443`.
- `domain` is the name on the certificate, lowercase, without a trailing dot.
- `source` is `files` (the owner's certificate files) or `acme`. `cert_file` and `key_file` are absolute paths when `source` is `files`, and empty otherwise. The key itself is never returned.
- `acme` is the stored ACME settings, present even for `files` (then its strings are empty and `staging` is false). `ca` is `letsencrypt`, `zerossl`, `googletrust` or `custom`; an empty `ca` means Let's Encrypt. `directory_url` is set only for `custom`, and is an `https://` URL with no user information, query or fragment. `staging` selects that authority's test directory. `email` is the account contact and is not a credential. `challenge` is `http-01` or `dns-01`. `http01_port` is omitted when unset, and unset means port 80; `0` means Core opens no port for the challenge. `dns_provider` is `cloudflare`, `alidns`, `tencentcloud` or `manual`, and is empty when the challenge is not `dns-01`.
- `credentials` says only whether a secret is stored (`set`). The secret is never returned. For `files` the object is empty. For ACME it always has `eab.kid` and `eab.hmac`. For `dns-01` it also has that provider's names: `cloudflare.api_token`; `alidns.access_key_id` and `alidns.access_key_secret`; `tencentcloud.secret_id` and `tencentcloud.secret_key`. `manual` adds none.
- `certificate` is null until a certificate is loaded. `issuer` and `subject` are the certificate's common names. `names` is the DNS names on the certificate (null when it has none). `serial` is lowercase hex. `staging` is true when the served certificate came from a test directory. `other_ca` is present and true only for an ACME certificate that was issued by a directory other than the one configured now; it keeps being served until a new order replaces it.
- `last_attempt_at` is when an order was last tried, or null. `last_renewal_at` and `next_renewal_at` are set for an enabled ACME configuration and are null when there is no time yet.
- `last_error` is null when there is no problem. Otherwise `code` and `message` describe it, `at` is when it was recorded, `warning` is true when the problem does not by itself stop a good certificate from being served (the name on the certificate does not match `domain`, or the order was cancelled), and `retry_at` is when Core will try again. `message` is Core's own text and never a credential. `code` is one of `files_unreadable`, `files_mismatch`, `files_expired`, `domain_mismatch`, `config_invalid`, `http01_port_denied`, `http01_port_busy`, `challenge_failed`, `dns_credentials`, `dns_zone_not_found`, `dns_propagation_timeout`, `dns_provider`, `manual_timeout`, `eab_required`, `eab_invalid`, `rate_limited`, `ca_unreachable`, `ca_timeout`, `ca_error`, `cancelled`, `store_failed`.
- `listen_error` is a short reason the HTTPS port could not be opened, or null.
- `pending` is null except during a manual TXT challenge. `kind` is `manual_txt` (add the record), `manual_txt_checking` (it was confirmed; DNS and the authority are checking) or `manual_txt_remove` (the order is done; the record can be removed). `order_id` identifies the order. `records` has one entry: `name` is the DNS name without a trailing dot, `value` is the TXT value. `expires_at` is set for `manual_txt` and is one hour after the record was published. `state` is `waiting_owner` only while `kind` is `manual_txt`.
- `propagation` is omitted except for a `dns-01` certificate that has been issued. `checked` means this host saw the TXT record. `assumed` means it did not, Core waited, and the authority validated anyway.
- `handshake_errors` counts failed TLS handshakes since this process started. A change of this number alone does not send `tls.changed`.

Errors:

- `503` TLS is not available in this Core

Events: none.

### GET /v1/update

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports the desktop app's updater, as that app last described it. A Core with no desktop report in the last 15 seconds answers with every flag false. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "supported": true,
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "available_version": "1.2.4",
  "ready": true,
  "downloading": false,
  "automatic": true,
  "error": false
}
```

- `supported` is true when this desktop can update itself.
- `version` is the desktop version that is running. An empty string means no fresh report.
- `available_version` is the version already downloaded and ready to install. Omitted when there is none.
- `ready` is true when that package can be installed. `downloading` is true while the desktop is still downloading it.
- `automatic` is true when the desktop will install a ready update by itself.
- `phase` is omitted while idle. `requested` means an install has been asked for. `waiting_steps` means a run or a memory review is still finishing. `waiting_persistence` means a run cannot be saved for a restart. `waiting_idle` means runs are going and will not be suspended. `restarting` means the desktop is restarting. Until the desktop has accepted an install request, `phase` stays `requested` even if the desktop has already moved on.
- `error` is true when the last download or restart failed. There is no error message. While an install request is still waiting for the desktop, `error` is false.
- A report older than 15 seconds is discarded. The body is then `supported`, `ready`, `downloading`, `automatic` and `error` all false, and `version` `""`, with `available_version` and `phase` omitted.

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### GET /v1/update/standalone

Auth: admin
Effect: Reports this standalone Core's own updater. A desktop-bundled Core and a development build do not have one. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "auto": true,
  "latest": "1.2.4",
  "last_check": "2026-10-14T03:00:00Z"
}
```

- `version` is the version of this Core.
- `auto` is true when a newer release found by the periodic check is installed by itself. It is read from the current settings on every call. `POST /v1/update/standalone` installs a newer release even when `auto` is false.
- `phase` is omitted while idle. `checking` is a check in progress. Then `downloading`, `waiting` (until a safe point to restart), `installing` and `restarting`.
- `latest` is the newest release the last check found. Omitted when that check found nothing newer.
- `last_check` is when a check last finished. Omitted until the first check finishes.
- `last_error` is the last check or install failure. Omitted when the last check succeeded. It can name a rate limit.
- `rate_limited_until` is when an anonymous rate limit resets. Omitted when no limit applies. It is read live, not frozen at `last_check`.

Errors:

- `404` not a standalone Core

Events: none.

### GET /v1/usage

Auth: any key
Effect: Returns recorded model-request attempts, newest first, plus totals for the same filter. Records do not contain prompts, replies or credentials. Deleting a conversation deletes its records. Editing or compacting a conversation does not.

Query: all optional.

- `session` matches that conversation, including every lane of it, or one lane when the value is the conversation id, a tilde, and the lane id.
- `model`, `provider`, `purpose`, `source` and `status` keep rows whose field is exactly that string.
- `from` and `to` are RFC3339. `from` is inclusive and `to` is exclusive (`started` >= `from` and `started` < `to`). When both are set, `to` must be after `from`. A date with no time is rejected.
- `origin` is `interactive`, `scheduled`, `compaction`, `memory_review` or `recap`. Omitted returns every bucket. It narrows the page, the summary, and the session, day and model groups. It does not narrow `breakdown.origins`.
- `executor` is omitted, `gyres`, `all`, `agents`, `codex`, `grok` or `claude`. Omitted and `gyres` keep Core's own rows (a missing `executor` counts as `gyres`). `agents` keeps every external-agent row. `all` keeps every row. `codex`, `grok` and `claude` keep that agent.
- `tz` is an integer number of minutes, from -840 to 840, the same value JavaScript's `getTimezoneOffset()` returns. It only names `breakdown.days`: that many minutes are subtracted from the UTC time (a negative value moves the clock forward) and the result is formatted `YYYY-MM-DD`. Omitted means `0`.
- `offset` is how many matching rows to skip. Omitted means `0`. Past the end, `records` is empty and `total` is still the full count.
- `limit` is the page size. Omitted or `0` means 100. Above 200 is treated as 200. The response `limit` is the value after that rule.

A row's origin bucket is `plugins` when `purpose` is anything other than empty, `chat`, `compaction`, `memory_review` or `recap`. Otherwise `compaction`, `memory_review` and `recap` stay in the bucket of that name. Otherwise `source` `scheduled` is `scheduled`, and everything else is `interactive`. `plugins` is not a legal `origin` query value.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "request_id": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
      "attempt": 1,
      "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-00-00_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef",
      "run_id": "abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789",
      "source": "interactive",
      "provider": "default",
      "model": "example-model",
      "format": "chat_completions",
      "purpose": "chat",
      "started": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
      "finished": "2026-10-14T12:00:02Z",
      "duration_ms": 2000,
      "status": "completed",
      "usage_state": "reported",
      "usage": {
        "cache_usage_reported": true,
        "input_tokens": 100,
        "output_tokens": 20,
        "cache_read_tokens": 40,
        "cache_write_tokens": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "cache_known": 1,
    "cache_input": 140,
    "cache_read": 40,
    "requests": 1,
    "known": 1,
    "partial": 0,
    "unknown": 0,
    "duration_ms": 2000,
    "tokens": { "input": 100, "output": 20, "cache_read": 40, "cache_write": 0 },
    "cost_usd": 0,
    "cost_known": 0
  },
  "breakdown": {
    "sessions": [
      {
        "session_id": "2026-10-14T12-00-00_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef",
        "requests": 1,
        "known": 1,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 100, "output": 20, "cache_read": 40, "cache_write": 0 },
        "last": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
        "models": ["example-model"],
        "origins": {
          "interactive": {
            "requests": 1,
            "known": 1,
            "partial": 0,
            "unknown": 0,
            "tokens": { "input": 100, "output": 20, "cache_read": 40, "cache_write": 0 }
          }
        },
        "cost_usd": 0
      }
    ],
    "days": [
      {
        "key": "2026-10-14",
        "requests": 1,
        "known": 1,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 100, "output": 20, "cache_read": 40, "cache_write": 0 },
        "last": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
        "cost_usd": 0
      }
    ],
    "models": [
      {
        "key": "example-model",
        "requests": 1,
        "known": 1,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 100, "output": 20, "cache_read": 40, "cache_write": 0 },
        "last": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
        "cost_usd": 0
      }
    ],
    "origins": [
      {
        "key": "interactive",
        "requests": 1,
        "known": 1,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 100, "output": 20, "cache_read": 40, "cache_write": 0 },
        "last": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
        "cost_usd": 0
      },
      {
        "key": "scheduled",
        "requests": 0,
        "known": 0,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0 },
        "cost_usd": 0
      },
      {
        "key": "compaction",
        "requests": 0,
        "known": 0,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0 },
        "cost_usd": 0
      },
      {
        "key": "memory_review",
        "requests": 0,
        "known": 0,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0 },
        "cost_usd": 0
      },
      {
        "key": "recap",
        "requests": 0,
        "known": 0,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0 },
        "cost_usd": 0
      },
      {
        "key": "plugins",
        "requests": 0,
        "known": 0,
        "partial": 0,
        "unknown": 0,
        "tokens": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0 },
        "cost_usd": 0
      }
    ]
  },
  "total": 1,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 100
}
```

- `records` is the page, newest `started` first. The same `started` is ordered by `id` descending. The array is empty, not null, when nothing matches. `total` counts every matching row, not just the page. `summary` and `breakdown` also cover every matching row.
- `version` is `1`. `id` is 32 lowercase hex and identifies one attempt. `request_id` is the logical request; retries share it and get a new `id` and a higher `attempt`. `session_id` is the conversation. `lane` is omitted for the main lane; otherwise `session_id` is the base conversation and the lane handle is `session_id`, a tilde, and `lane`. `run_id` is the run. `schedule_id` is set when a scheduled task started the run.
- `source` is the label the turn was started with, such as `interactive`, `scheduled` or `background`. `provider` and `model` are what the request was sent to. `fallback_from` is `provider id/model` of the conversation's model when a fallback model served this request instead, and is omitted otherwise.
- `format` is `chat_completions` or `responses` for Core's own request. For an external-agent row it is the agent name, `codex`, `grok` or `claude`.
- `purpose` is why the request was made: `chat`, `compaction`, `memory_review`, `recap`, or a hook or plugin purpose. Older rows may omit it; that means chat.
- `caller` is omitted for Core's own requests. It is `hook:` plus a handler id, or `key:` plus an access key id, when the request was made for that caller.
- `started` is when the attempt began. `finished` is omitted until it ends. `duration_ms` is the model call, not tool time, and is `0` until the attempt finishes.
- `status` is `running` while the attempt is open, then `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. An attempt still `running` when Core restarts is returned as `interrupted`.
- `usage_state` is `reported` when a successful attempt included usage, `partial` when a failed or cancelled attempt included some, and `unknown` when none arrived. Do not read zeros as a bill when `usage_state` is `unknown`. A restarted `running` attempt is returned as `unknown`. An external-agent row is `reported` when its `status` is `completed` and `partial` otherwise.
- `usage.input_tokens` is non-cached input. `output_tokens` includes reasoning tokens when the provider includes them there. `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens` are separate. `cache_usage_reported` is true when the provider reported cache figures, and is omitted when false.
- `executor` is omitted for Core (read those rows as `gyres`) and is `codex`, `grok` or `claude` for an external agent. `cost_usd` is that agent's own estimate for the turn, and `cost_source` is `agent_estimate`. Both are omitted when the agent gave no estimate. Core does not price its own requests.
- `error` on a failed Core attempt is `模型请求失败；详情见所属对话`. On a cancelled Core attempt it is `请求已取消`. `failure`, when present, is the same shape as a request error's `failure` (`code`, `message`, `http_status`, `details`) and is a sanitised provider error. A cancelled attempt omits `failure`.
- `diagnostics`, when present, compares this attempt with the previous one for the same conversation and purpose. It holds hashes only, never the prompt. `kind` is `baseline`, `unchanged`, `append_only`, `changed` or `limited`. `changes` lists what moved: `route`, `context`, `system`, `tools`, `parameters`, `history`. `previous_attempt` is the earlier attempt id. `first_difference` names the first item that differs. `common_items`, `item_count` and `previous_items` count items. `request_bytes` is the payload size. `body_hash`, `system_hash`, `tools_hash` and `parameters_hash` are hex digests. `context_epoch` names the context snapshot. `limited` is true when the comparison stopped at 4096 items.
- `summary.requests`, `known`, `partial` and `unknown` count rows by `usage_state` (`known` is `reported`; anything other than `reported` or `partial` counts as `unknown`). `tokens` sums every matching row: `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`. `duration_ms` sums the attempts. `cache_known` counts rows that are `reported` and have `cache_usage_reported`. For those rows only, `cache_input` is input plus cache read plus cache write, and `cache_read` is the cache-read sum. `cost_usd` sums agent estimates, and `cost_known` counts the rows that had one.
- `breakdown.sessions` is one object per conversation, largest token total first, then latest `last`, then `session_id`. `models` on a session is the distinct model names, sorted. `origins` on a session has only the buckets that had rows. `cost_usd` sums that session's agent estimates.
- `breakdown.days` is sorted by `key` ascending. `key` is the `YYYY-MM-DD` from `tz`. `breakdown.models` is one object per model name (`key`), largest token total first.
- `breakdown.origins` always has six objects, in this order, even when every count is zero and even when `origin` filtered the rest of the response: `interactive`, `scheduled`, `compaction`, `memory_review`, `recap`, `plugins`. A group has `key`, `requests`, `known`, `partial`, `unknown`, `tokens`, `cost_usd`, and `last` (omitted when the group is empty).
- `days`, `models` and `sessions` are empty arrays when they have no rows. They are not null.

Errors:

- `400` invalid time filter
- `400` invalid pagination (`offset` or `limit` is not a whole number, or is negative)
- `400` invalid time range (`to` is not after `from`)
- `400` invalid origin
- `400` invalid executor
- `400` invalid time zone
- `500` cannot read usage records

Events: none.

### GET /v1/version

Auth: any key
Effect: Reports this Core's build version and the interface version. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

```json
{ "version": "dev", "api_version": 1 }
```

- `version` is the Core build version. A development build sends `dev`. A release build sends its version string.
- `api_version` is an integer. It goes up by one on every breaking change listed in CHANGELOG.md. Additions do not change it. A frontend compares it with the `api_version` it was built for. A Core that answers this route with `404` is older than this spec.

Errors: none.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/browser-runtime/install

Auth: any key
Effect: Starts installing the managed browser, if it is not already installed or already installing. The call returns as soon as the job is accepted. Poll `GET /v1/browser-runtime` for progress. A second call while an install is running, or while the browser is already ready, does not start another install.

Request: no body.

Response: `202`

The body is the same object as `GET /v1/browser-runtime`. When a new install starts, `state` is `installing` and `phase` is `checking` until the job moves on. The install gives up after 15 minutes.

Errors:

- `503` the managed browser is not running in this Core. The body is only `{"error":"Browser unavailable"}`, with no `failure`.
- `400` the install could not start. The body is only `{"error":"<reason>"}`, with no `failure`. When this host cannot install it and the browser is not already present, the reason is `automatic installation supports macOS Apple silicon, Linux amd64/arm64, and Windows amd64/arm64`. A later GET then has `state` `error` and the same text in `error`.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/code-runtime/install

Auth: any key
Effect: Starts installing the managed code runtime, if it is not already installed or already installing. The call returns as soon as the job is accepted. Poll `GET /v1/code-runtime`. A second call while an install is running, or while a ready runtime file is present, does not start another install.

Request: no body.

Response: `200`

The body is the same object as `GET /v1/code-runtime`. When a new install starts, `state` is `installing`. The install gives up after 15 minutes.

Errors:

- `503` the code runtime is not running in this Core. The body is only `{"error":"code runtime unavailable"}`, with no `failure`.
- `503` the install could not start. The body is only `{"error":"<reason>"}`, with no `failure`. On a host other than macOS Apple silicon the reason is `managed Bun currently supports macOS arm64`. A later GET then has `state` `error` and the same text in `error`.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/identity/challenge

Auth: none
Effect: Proves that this Core holds a given access key, without the client sending that key. A client runs it before it sends its key to an address it is not sure about: an address found on the local network (the `_gyres._tcp` TXT `id` is public, so anything can claim it), or a saved address that may now belong to another device. Changes nothing. Nothing about the request is logged. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request:

```json
{
  "key_id": "0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "nonce": "000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f",
  "target": "http://192.0.2.10:15100"
}
```

- `key_id` (string, required, 1–64 characters) names the client's key without revealing it. For a key of the form `gyres_<id>_<secret>` it is `<id>`. For any other key it is `legacy-` followed by the first 24 lowercase hex characters of the SHA-256 of the whole key. Another Core holding a peer key `gyp_<id>_<secret>` (see [Bot peers](peers.md)) names it `peer-<id>`; the proof is computed the same way from that key.
- `nonce` (string, required) is 32 to 128 lowercase hex characters, an even number, fresh random for every challenge (send at least 16 random bytes; 32 is recommended).
- `target` (string, required, at most 512 bytes, no control characters) is the `http` or `https` origin the client sent this request to: scheme, host and optional port, no path other than `/`, no query, fragment or user info.
- The body is one JSON object of at most 4096 bytes with only these fields.

Response: `200`

```json
{
  "instance_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "target_ok": true,
  "proof": "d9600a2ec1215ce953bcdd7ef1ea0893fde6ce3012a0f22c1acfa0dd97c9c761"
}
```

- `instance_id` is the same value as in `GET /v1/identity`.
- `target_ok` is true when `target` is one of the origins `GET /v1/identity` lists in `addresses` at this moment. Scheme and host compare without case and a missing port counts as 80 or 443. Forwarding headers are not used.
- `proof` is 64 lowercase hex characters: `HMAC-SHA256(k, m)`, where `k` is the 32-byte SHA-256 of the full access key (UTF-8) and `m` is the UTF-8 text `gyres-identity-v1`, `nonce`, `instance_id`, `target` (exactly as sent) and `1` or `0` for `target_ok`, joined with `\n` (one newline byte, none at the end).
- To verify, compute the same HMAC from your stored key, the nonce you sent, the target you sent and the `instance_id` and `target_ok` received, compare in constant time, and check `instance_id` against the one you saved for this Core. Send the key only when it matches. A relay that forwards your challenge to the real Core gets `target_ok` false, since your target names the relay, and cannot change the flag without breaking the proof. Accept `target_ok` false only for an address you already trust for other reasons (one you saved, for example behind a proxy or a port forward), never for a newly discovered one.
- An unknown or malformed `key_id` answers the same way, with a proof that does not verify under any key, so the route does not reveal which key ids exist. A revoked or replaced key still gets a valid proof; sending it then returns `401`.
- Test vectors: [identity-proof-vectors.json](../identity-proof-vectors.json).

Errors:

- `400` invalid request (body is not one JSON object of the fields above, a field is missing or malformed, or the body is larger than 4096 bytes)
- `429` too many attempts; try again later. More than 60 challenges from one client address within one minute; the address is taken under the same trusted-proxy rules as pairing. The response sets `Retry-After: 60`.
- `404` identity proof is not available (Core runs without access keys). A Core older than this route answers `401`, because it needs a key for every unknown route.

Events: none.

### POST /v1/tls/issue

Auth: admin
Effect: Asks Core to obtain or renew the ACME certificate in the background. Saving HTTPS settings does not start an order; this call does. The first certificate, and a certificate from a newly chosen authority, come only from this call. The response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Request:

```json
{ "force": false }
```

- `force` (boolean, optional) renews even when the current certificate is not due yet. Omitted means false. An empty body is accepted and means false. Unknown fields are ignored. The body is at most 65536 bytes.

Response: `202`

The body is the same object as `GET /v1/tls`, read just after the order was accepted. With no certificate yet, `state` is `issuing`. A renewal of a certificate that is already being served can stay `active` until the order moves it. A refused call does not send `tls.changed`. An accepted call sends it when the status changed, and the order sends it again whenever the status changes after that. `handshake_errors` alone does not. Read `GET /v1/tls` again after the event.

Errors:

- `503` TLS is not available in this Core
- `400` invalid json (a body was sent and it is not JSON, or it is larger than 65536 bytes)
- `409` the order was not started. The body has `error` and `code`, and no `failure`:

```json
{ "error": "the certificate is not due for renewal", "code": "not_due" }
```
